\text{(distinct)}\end{subarray}}(W_{i_{1}i_{2}}+\bar{\Omega}_{i_{1}i_{2}})(W_{i_{2}i_{3}}+\bar{\Omega}_{i_{2}i_{3}})...(W_{i_{m}i_{1}}+\bar{\Omega}_{i_{m}i_{1}}), $$

where $W_{ij}=A_{ij}-\Omega_{ij}$ and $\bar{\Omega}_{ij}=\Omega_{ij}-\alpha_{0}$ for all $i\neq j$ . Then, direct calculations show that:

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{1}\left[\bar{U}_{n}^{(m)}\right] \displaystyle=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i_{1},...,i_{m}\\
\text{(distinct)}\end{subarray}}\bar{\Omega}_{i_{1}i_{2}}\bar{\Omega}_{i_{2}i_{3}}...\bar{\Omega}_{i_{m}i_{1}} \displaystyle=\sum_{i_{1},...,i_{m}}\bar{\Omega}_{i_{1}i_{2}}\bar{\Omega}_{i_{2}i_{3}}...\bar{\Omega}_{i_{m}i_{1}}-\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i_{1},...,i_{m}\\
\text{(not distinct)}\end{subarray}}\bar{\Omega}_{i_{1}i_{2}}\bar{\Omega}_{i_{2}i_{3}}...\bar{\Omega}_{i_{m}i_{1}} \displaystyle=\mbox{Tr}(\bar{\Omega}^{m})-O\left(n^{m-1}\|M\|^{m}\right)=\mbox{Tr}\left((\Pi M\Pi^{\prime})^{m}\right)-O\left(n^{m-1}\|M\|^{m}\right) \displaystyle=n^{m}\mbox{Tr}\left((MG)^{m}\right)-O\left(n^{m-1}\|M\|^{m}\right)\asymp n^{m}\|MG\|^{m}-O\left(n^{m-1}\|M\|^{m}\right). $$

Since we have assumed that $\|G\|,\|G^{-1}\|<c$ by condition (3.4), we obtain that

$$ \left|\mathbb{E}_{1}\left[\bar{U}_{n}^{(m)}\right]\right|\asymp n^{m}\|P-\alpha_{0}\bm{1}_{K}\bm{1}_{K}^{\prime}\|^{m}. $$

∎

The results in Lemma C.2 allow us to compute the SNR for the length- $m$ Signed Cycle statistic. We derive the SNR assuming that the null variance dominates the alternative variance. Thus,

$$ \displaystyle SNR\left(\bar{U}_{n}^{(m)}\right) \displaystyle=\frac{\left|\mathbb{E}_{1}\left[\bar{U}_{n}^{(m)}\right]-\mathbb{E}_{0}\left[\bar{U}_{n}^{(m)}\right]\right|}{\sqrt{\max\left\{\mbox{Var}_{0}\left(\bar{U}_{n}^{(m)}\right),\mbox{Var}_{1}\left(\bar{U}_{n}^{(m)}\right)\right\}}}\asymp\frac{\left|\mathbb{E}_{1}\left[\bar{U}_{n}^{(m)}\right]\right|}{\sqrt{\mbox{Var}_{0}\left(\bar{U}_{n}^{(m)}\right)}} \displaystyle\asymp\frac{n^{m}\|M\|^{m}}{n^{m/2}\alpha_{n}^{m/2}}=\tau_{n}^{m/4}. $$

Similar to our results in Theorem 3.3, there may be instances in which the alternative variance dominates the null variance. In these cases, the SNR still depends on powers of $\tau_{n}$ , and the detection boundary is unchanged; details are omitted.

## Appendix D Proof of Theorem 3.1

Write $\varphi_{n}^{DC}=(X_{n}-n)/\sqrt{2n}$ and $\psi_{n}^{SQ}=Q_{n}/(2\sqrt{2}n^{2}\hat{\alpha}_{n}^{2})$ . We aim to show that $(\psi_{n}^{DC},\psi_{n}^{SQ})$ converges to $\mathcal{N}(0,I_{2})$ in distribution. By the Cramér-Wold theorem, it suffices to show that

$$ u\cdot\psi_{n}^{DC}+v\cdot\psi_{n}^{SQ}\quad\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{\mathcal{L}}\quad\mathcal{N}(0,1),\qquad\mbox{for any $u,v\in\mathbb{R}$ with $u^{2}+v^{2}=1$}. $$

Below, we first study the null distribution of $\psi_{n}^{DC}$ and $\psi_{n}^{SQ}$ respectively. These analyses produce useful intermediate results. We then use them to show the desirable claim in (D.1).

### D.1 Proof of the null distribution of $\psi_{n}^{DC}$

We aim to show that

$$ \varphi_{n}^{DC}=\frac{X_{n}-n}{\sqrt{2n}}\quad\xrightarrow{d}\quad\mathcal{N}(0,1). $$

First, we derive an equivalent expression of $X_{n}$ . Let $\hat{T}_{n}=\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}(A_{ik}-\hat{\alpha}_{n})(A_{jk}-\hat{\alpha}_{n})$ , where $\hat{\alpha}_{n}$ is the same as in the definition of $X_{n}$ . We claim that

$$ X_{n}=n+\frac{\hat{T}_{n}}{(n-1)\hat{\alpha}_{n}(1-\hat{\alpha}_{n})}. $$

We now show (D.3). By definition,

$$ X_{n}=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac{(d_{i}-\hbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.5pt\kern 2.15277pt\hbox{\kern-1.00006pt$d$\kern-1.00006pt}}})^{2}}{(n-1)\hat{\alpha}_{n}(1-\hat{\alpha}_{n})}, d $$

where

$$ \displaystyle\hat{\alpha}_{n}=\frac{1}{n(n-1)}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}A\bm{1}_{n} \displaystyle d=A\bm{1}_{n} \displaystyle\hbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.5pt\kern 2.15277pt\hbox{\kern-1.00006pt$d$\kern-1.00006pt}}}=\frac{1}{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}A\bm{1}_{n}=(n-1)\hat{\alpha}_{n}. d $$

We expand $X_{n}$ into a sum of two terms that can be easily studied:

$$ \displaystyle X_{n} \displaystyle=\frac{\|d\|_{2}^{2}-n\hbox{\vbox{\hrule height=0.5pt\kern 2.15277pt\hbox{\kern-1.00006pt$d$\kern-1.00006pt}}}^{2}}{(n-1)\hat{\alpha}_{n}(1-\hat{\alpha}_{n})}=\frac{\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}A^{2}\bm{1}_{n}}{(n-1)\hat{\alpha}_{n}(1-\hat{\alpha}_{n})}-\frac{n(n-1)\hat{\alpha}_{n}}{1-\hat{\alpha}_{n}}. d $$

We can compute $\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}A^{2}\bm{1}_{n}$ as follows:

$$ \displaystyle\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}A^{2}\bm{1}_{n} \displaystyle=\sum_{i,j}(A^{2})_{ij}=\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}A\bm{1}_{n}+\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}A_{ik}A_{jk}=n(n-1)\hat{\alpha}_{n}+\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}A_{ik}A_{jk}. $$

Hence we further reexpress $X_{n}$ as

$$ \displaystyle X_{n} \displaystyle=\frac{\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}A_{ik}A_{jk}}{(n-1)\hat{\alpha}_{n}(1-\hat{\alpha}_{n})}+\frac{n-n(n-1)\hat{\alpha}_{n}}{1-\hat{\alpha}_{n}}. $$

Recalling that $\hat{T}_{n}=\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}(A_{ik}-\hat{\alpha}_{n})(A_{jk}-\hat{\alpha}_{n})$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}A_{ik}A_{jk} \displaystyle=\hat{T}_{n}+2(n-2)\hat{\alpha}_{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}A\bm{1}_{n}-n(n-1)(n-2)\hat{\alpha}^{2}_{n} \displaystyle=\hat{T}_{n}+n(n-1)(n-2)\hat{\alpha}_{n}^{2}. $$

It follows that

$$ \displaystyle X_{n}-n \displaystyle=\frac{\hat{T}_{n}+n(n-1)(n-2)\hat{\alpha}_{n}^{2}}{(n-1)\hat{\alpha}_{n}(1-\hat{\alpha}_{n})}+\frac{n-n(n-1)\hat{\alpha}_{n}}{1-\hat{\alpha}_{n}}-n=\frac{\hat{T}_{n}}{(n-1)\hat{\alpha}_{n}(1-\hat{\alpha}_{n})}. $$

This proves (D.3).

Next, we introduce an ideal counterpart to $\hat{T}_{n}$ , $T_{n}=\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}(A_{ik}-\alpha_{n})(A_{jk}-\alpha_{n})$ . Direct computations show that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[T_{n}]=0 \displaystyle\text{Var}(T_{n}) \displaystyle=2n(n-1)(n-2)\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}. $$

Thus

$$ \text{Var}\left(\frac{T_{n}}{(n-1)\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}\right)=\frac{2n(n-2)}{n-1}. $$

Combining it with (D.3), we obtain

$$ \frac{X_{n}-n}{\sqrt{2n}}=\left(\frac{\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}{\hat{\alpha}_{n}(1-\hat{\alpha}_{n}}\right)\left(\frac{\hat{T}_{n}}{T_{n}}\right)\left(\frac{n-2}{n-1}\right)^{1/2}\left(\frac{\frac{T_{n}}{(n-1)\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}{\sqrt{\frac{2n(n-2)}{(n-1)}}}\right). $$

Define

$$ \displaystyle U_{n}=\frac{\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}{\hat{\alpha}_{n}(1-\hat{\alpha}_{n})} \displaystyle V_{n}=\frac{\hat{T}_{n}}{T_{n}} \displaystyle Z_{n}=\frac{\frac{T_{n}}{(n-1)\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}{\sqrt{\frac{2n(n-2)}{(n-1)}}}. $$

We have the following decomposition:

$$ \frac{X_{n}-n}{\sqrt{2n}}=\left(\frac{n-2}{n-1}\right)^{1/2}U_{n}V_{n}Z_{n}. $$

Below, we study $U_{n}$ , $V_{n}$ , and $Z_{n}$ , separately.

Consider $U_{n}$ . Note that

$$ \hat{\alpha}_{n}=\frac{1}{n(n-1)}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}A\bm{1}_{n}=\frac{2}{n(n-1)}\sum_{i<j}A_{ij}, $$

where $(A_{ij})_{i<j}$ are i.i.d. Bernoulli random variables with mean $\alpha_{n}$ . By the Weak Law of Large Numbers we obtain that

$$ \frac{\hat{\alpha}_{n}}{\alpha_{n}}=\frac{2}{n(n-1)}\sum_{i<j}\frac{A_{ij}}{\alpha_{n}}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}1, $$

from which we conclude that $U_{n}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}1$ .

Consider $V_{n}$ . Note that

$$ \displaystyle\hat{T}_{n}-T_{n} \displaystyle=\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}(A_{ik}-\hat{\alpha}_{n})(A_{jk}-\hat{\alpha}_{n})-\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}(A_{ik}-\alpha_{n})(A_{jk}-\alpha_{n}) \displaystyle=\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}(\alpha_{n}-\hat{\alpha}_{n})(A_{ik}+A_{jk}-\alpha_{n}-\hat{\alpha}_{n}) \displaystyle=(\alpha_{n}-\hat{\alpha}_{n})\left[2\left(\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}A_{ik}\right)-n(n-1)(n-2)(\alpha_{n}+\hat{\alpha}_{n})\right] \displaystyle=(\alpha_{n}-\hat{\alpha}_{n})\left[2(n-2)\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}A\bm{1}_{n}-n(n-1)(n-2)(\alpha_{n}+\hat{\alpha}_{n})\right] \displaystyle=(\alpha_{n}-\hat{\alpha}_{n})\left[2n(n-1)(n-2)\hat{\alpha}_{n}-n(n-1)(n-2)(\alpha_{n}+\hat{\alpha}_{n})\right] \displaystyle=-n(n-1)(n-2)(\alpha_{n}-\hat{\alpha}_{n})^{2}. $$

It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\left|\frac{\hat{T}_{n}-T_{n}}{T_{n}}\right| \displaystyle=\left|\frac{n(n-1)(n-2)(\alpha_{n}-\hat{\alpha}_{n})^{2}}{T_{n}}\right| \displaystyle=\sqrt{\frac{2(n-2)}{n(n-1)}}\left(\sqrt{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}}\frac{\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\alpha_{n}}{\sqrt{\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}\right)^{2}\left|\frac{\sqrt{\frac{2n(n-2)}{n-1}}}{\frac{T_{n}}{(n-1)\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}\right| \displaystyle=\sqrt{\frac{n-2}{2(n-1)}}\left(\sqrt{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}}\frac{\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\alpha_{n}}{\sqrt{\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}\right)^{2}\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}|Z_{n}|}. $$

Note that $\hat{\alpha}_{n}=\frac{2}{n(n-1)}\sum_{i<j}A(i,j)$ , where $A_{ij}$ are i.i.d. Bernoulli random variables with mean $\alpha_{n}$ . By the Central Limit Theorem,

$$ \sqrt{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}}\frac{\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\alpha_{n}}{\sqrt{\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{\mathcal{L}}\mathcal{N}(0,1). $$

We will show later that $Z_{n}\xrightarrow{\mathcal{L}}\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ . It follows that $(\sqrt{n}|Z_{n}|)^{-1}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0$ (by Slutsky’s theorem) and we conclude by Slutsky’s theorem again that

$$ \left|\frac{\hat{T}_{n}-T_{n}}{T_{n}}\right|\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0, $$

which shows that $V_{n}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}1$ .

Consider $Z_{n}$ . We define

$$ I_{m}=\{(i,j,k)\in\llbracket 1,m\rrbracket^{3}\text{ s.t. $i,j,k$ are distinct}\}, $$

and the following quantities for $m\in\llbracket 1,n\rrbracket$

$$ \displaystyle T_{n,m} \displaystyle=\sum_{(i,j,k)\in I_{m}}W_{ik}W_{jk},\qquad\text{ and }\qquad T_{n,0}=0, \displaystyle Z_{n,m} \displaystyle=\sqrt{\frac{n-1}{2n(n-2)}}\frac{T_{n,m}}{(n-1)\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})},\qquad\text{ and }\qquad Z_{n,0}=0. $$

Consider the filtration $\{\mathcal{F}_{n,m}\}_{1\leq m\leq n}$ with $\mathcal{F}_{n,m}=\sigma\{W_{ij},(i,j)\in\llbracket 1,m\rrbracket^{2}\}$ for all $m\in\llbracket 1,n\rrbracket$ , $\mathcal{F}_{n,0}=\{\Omega,\emptyset\}$ (where $\Omega$ denotes the sample space). It is straightforward to see that for all $0\leq m\leq n$ , $Z_{n,m}$ is $\mathcal{F}_{n,m}$ -measurable, $\mathbb{E}[|Z_{n,m}|]<\infty$ and $\mathbb{E}\left[T_{n,m+1}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m}\right]=T_{n,m}$ . This shows that $\{Z_{n,m}\}_{1\leq m\leq n}$ is a martingale with respect to $\{\mathcal{F}_{n,m}\}_{1\leq m\leq n}$ . Define the martingale difference sequence, for all $m=1,...,n$

$$ X_{n,m}=Z_{n,m}-Z_{n,m-1}. $$

With these notations we have $Z_{n}\equiv Z_{n,n}=\sum_{m=1}^{n}X_{n,m}$ . Provided the following two conditions are met

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}1, \displaystyle\forall\epsilon>0,\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}\bm{1}\{|X_{n,m}>\epsilon|\}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0, $$

we conclude using the Martingale Central Limit Theorem that $Z_{n}\xrightarrow{\mathcal{L}}\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ .

So far, we have shown that $Z_{n}\xrightarrow{\mathcal{L}}\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ , $U_{n}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}1$ and $V_{n}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}1$ . We plug them into (D.4). Then, (D.2) follows immediately from Slutsky’s theorem.

The only remaining steps are to verify that (D.7) and (D.8) are indeed satisfied.

Proof of Equation (D.7): It suffices to show that

$$ \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right]=1, $$

and

$$ \text{Var}\left(\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right)\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0. $$

First, we prove Equation (D.9). For notational convenience we write

$$ C_{n}:=(n-1)\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})\sqrt{\frac{2n(n-2)}{n-1}}. $$

It follows that for all $n\in\mathbb{N}^{*}$ and $m\in\llbracket 1,n\rrbracket$

$$ C_{n}X_{n,m}=C_{n}(Z_{n,m}-Z_{n,m-1})=T_{n,m}-T_{n,m-1}=\sum_{(i,j,k)\in I_{m}\setminus I_{m-1}}W_{ik}W_{jk}. $$

Triplets in $I_{m}\setminus I_{m-1}$ are such that one of the nodes is $m$ : either one of the wingnodes $\{i,j\}$ , or the centernode $k$ . Hence,

$$ C_{n}X_{n,m}=2\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq j,k\leq m-1\\
j\neq k\end{subarray}}W_{mk}W_{jk}+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i,j\leq m-1\\
i\neq j\end{subarray}}W_{im}W_{jm}. $$

As a result (in the following, summations are all up to $m-1$ )

$$ C_{n}^{2}X_{n,m}^{2}=4\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}k\neq j\\
i\neq l\end{subarray}}W_{mk}W_{jk}W_{mi}W_{il}+4\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}k\neq j\\
i\neq l\end{subarray}}W_{mk}W_{jk}W_{im}W_{lm}+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i\neq j\\
k\neq l\end{subarray}}W_{im}W_{jm}W_{km}W_{lm}. $$

It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[C_{n}^{2}X_{n,m}^{2}| \displaystyle\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]=4\sum_{k\neq j;\;i\neq l}W_{jk}W_{il}\mathbb{E}\left[W_{mk}W_{mi}\right]+4\sum_{k\neq j;\;i\neq l}W_{jk}\mathbb{E}\left[W_{im}W_{km}W_{lm}\right] \displaystyle+\sum_{i\neq j;\;k\neq l}\mathbb{E}\left[W_{im}W_{jm}W_{km}W_{lm}\right] \displaystyle= \displaystyle 4\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})\sum_{i}\sum_{j\neq i,l\neq i}W_{ij}W_{il}+2(m-1)(m-2)\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2} \displaystyle= \displaystyle 4\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})\sum_{(i,j,l)\in I_{m-1}}W_{ij}W_{il}+4\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})\sum_{i\neq j}W_{ij}^{2} \displaystyle+2(m-1)(m-2)\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2} \displaystyle= \displaystyle 4\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})\Bigl(T_{n,m-1}+\sum_{i\neq j}W_{ij}^{2}\Bigr)+2(m-1)(m-2)\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}. $$

Let $\bm{1}_{n,m}\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ be a vector whose $m$ first entries are 1, and whose remaining entries are 0. Define

$$ \hat{\alpha}_{n,m}:=\frac{\bm{1}_{n,m}^{\prime}A\bm{1}_{n,m}}{m(m-1)}. $$

By direct calculations,

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{i\neq j}W_{ij}^{2} \displaystyle=\sum_{i\neq j}(A_{ij}-\alpha_{n})^{2}=\sum_{i\neq j}\left[A_{ij}(1-2\alpha_{n})+\alpha_{n}^{2}\right] \displaystyle=(m-1)(m-2)\alpha_{n}^{2}+(1-2\alpha_{n})\sum_{i,j}A_{ij} \displaystyle=(m-1)(m-2)\alpha_{n}^{2}+(1-2\alpha_{n})(m-1)(m-2)\hat{\alpha}_{n,m-1}. $$

We plug the above equation into (D.12) to get

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[C_{n}^{2}X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}] \displaystyle=4\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})T_{n,m-1}+2(m-1)(m-2)\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2} \displaystyle+4(m-1)(m-2)\alpha_{n}^{3}(1-\alpha_{n}) \displaystyle+4(m-1)(m-2)\alpha_{n}\hat{\alpha}_{n,m-1}(1-\alpha_{n})(1-2\alpha_{n}). $$

It follows that

$$ \displaystyle C_{n}^{2}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}] \displaystyle=4\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})\sum_{m=1}^{n}T_{n,m-1} \displaystyle+\left[2\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}+4\alpha_{n}^{3}(1-\alpha_{n})\right]\sum_{m=1}^{n}(m-1)(m-2) \displaystyle+4\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})(1-2\alpha_{n})\sum_{m=1}^{n}(m-1)(m-2)\hat{\alpha}_{n,m-1}. $$

Recall that $\mathbb{E}[T_{n,m-1}]=\sum_{(i,j,k)\in I_{m-1}}\mathbb{E}[W_{ik}W_{jk}]=\sum_{(i,k)\in I_{m-1}}\mathbb{E}[W_{ik}^{2}]=\frac{(m-1)(m-2)}{2}\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})$ . Additionally, $\mathbb{E}[\hat{\alpha}_{n,m-1}]=\alpha_{n}$ . We thus have

$$ \displaystyle C_{n}^{2}\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right] \displaystyle=2\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}\sum_{m=1}^{n}(m-1)(m-2) \displaystyle+\left[2\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}+4\alpha_{n}^{3}(1-\alpha_{n})\right]\sum_{m=1}^{n}(m-1)(m-2) \displaystyle+4\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})(1-2\alpha_{n})\sum_{m=1}^{n}\alpha_{n}(m-1)(m-2) \displaystyle=6\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}\sum_{m=1}^{n}(m-1)(m-2) \displaystyle=2\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}n(n-1)(n-2)=C_{n}^{2}. $$

This proves (D.9).

Second, we prove Equation (D.10). In the second line of (D.12), we have seen that

$$ \displaystyle C_{n}^{2}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}] \displaystyle=4\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})\sum_{k}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i\neq j\leq m-1\\
i\neq k,j\neq k\end{subarray}}W_{ki}W_{kj}+2(m-1)(m-2)\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2} \displaystyle=8\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})\sum_{k}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i<j\leq m-1\\
i\neq k,j\neq k\end{subarray}}W_{ki}W_{kj}+2(m-1)(m-2)\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}. $$

As a result,

$$ \displaystyle\text{Var}\left(C_{n}^{2}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right)\leq 64\alpha_{n}^{2}\text{Var}\left(\sum_{m=1}^{n}\sum_{k}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i<j\leq m-1\\
i\neq k,j\neq k\end{subarray}}W_{ki}W_{kj}\right). $$

Recall that in the previous sums, summation over the indices $i,j,k$ ranges from $1$ to $m-1$ . We rearrange the terms of the sums in order to facilitate the computation of the variance. Instead of summing over the order $m$ , then over centernodes $k$ ranging from $1$ to $m-1$ , and finally over wingnodes $i,j$ also ranging from $1$ to $m-1$ , we now sum over centernodes $k$ ranging from $1$ to $n-1$ , wingnodes ranging from $1$ to $n-1$ , and finally over orders $m>\max{(i,j,k)}$ .

$$ \displaystyle\text{Var}\left(C_{n}^{2}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right)\leq 64\alpha_{n}^{2}\text{Var}\left(\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i<j\leq n-1\\
i\neq k,j\neq k\end{subarray}}\sum_{m>\max(i,j,k)}W_{ki}W_{kj}\right) \displaystyle\leq 64\alpha_{n}^{2}n^{2}\text{Var}\left(\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i<j\leq n-1\\
i\neq k,j\neq k\end{subarray}}W_{ki}W_{kj}\right)=64\alpha_{n}^{2}n^{2}\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\text{Var}\left(\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i<j\leq n-1\\
i\neq k,j\neq k\end{subarray}}W_{ki}W_{kj}\right), $$

where the last equality comes from the fact that in the above sum, terms corresponding to different values of the index $k$ are uncorrelated. As a result

$$ \text{Var}\left(C_{n}^{2}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right)\leq 64\alpha_{n}^{2}n^{2}\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i<j\leq n-1\\
1\leq u<v\leq n-1\\
i,j,u,v\neq k\end{subarray}}\text{Cov}(W_{ki}W_{kj},W_{ku}W_{kv}). $$

We examine the possible cases for $\text{Cov}(W_{ki}W_{kj},W_{ku}W_{kv})$ .

- • Case 1: $(i,j)=(u,v)$ , then $\text{Cov}(W_{ki}W_{kj},W_{ku}W_{kv})=\text{Var}(W_{ki}W_{kj})=\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}$ .

- • Case 2: $i=u,j\neq v$ or $i\neq u,j=v$ , then $\text{Cov}(W_{ki}W_{kj},W_{ku}W_{kv})=0$ .

- • All other cases: $\text{Cov}(W_{ki}W_{kj},W_{ku}W_{kv})=0$ .

It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\text{Var}\left(C_{n}^{2}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right) \displaystyle\leq 64\alpha_{n}^{2}n^{2}\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i<j\leq n-1\\
i,j\neq k\end{subarray}}\text{Var}(W_{ki}W_{kj}) \displaystyle=64\alpha_{n}^{2}n^{2}\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i<j\leq n-1\\
i,j\neq k\end{subarray}}\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}\leq 32\alpha_{n}^{4}n^{5}. $$

Hence

$$ \displaystyle\text{Var}\left(\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right) \displaystyle\leq\frac{32\alpha_{n}^{4}n^{5}}{C_{n}^{4}}=\frac{1}{n}\left(\frac{n^{4}}{(n-1)^{2}(n-2)^{2}}\right)\left(\frac{8}{(1-\alpha_{n})^{4}}\right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0. $$

This proves (D.10).

Proof of Equation (D.8): Notice that by the Cauchy-Schwarz and Markov inequalities we obtain the following upper bound

$$ \displaystyle\left|\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}\bm{1}\{|X_{n,m}>\epsilon|\}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right| \displaystyle\leq\sum_{m=1}^{n}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{4}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]}\sqrt{\mathbb{P}(|X_{n,m}|>\epsilon|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1})} \displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{\epsilon^{2}}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{4}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]. $$

Thus it suffices to show that $\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{4}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0$ . Since these random variables are all non-negative, we will equivalently show that

$$ \sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{4}]=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{4}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right]\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0. $$

We now show (D.22). Recall that (see (D.11))

$$ \displaystyle C_{n}X_{n,m} \displaystyle=2\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq m-1}W_{im}W_{jm}+2\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq m-1}W_{ij}W_{jm} \displaystyle=2\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq m-1}W_{jm}(W_{ij}+W_{im}). $$

Then (with summations ranging from $1$ to $m-1$ )

$$ C_{n}^{4}X_{n,m}^{4}=16\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i<j\\
u<v\\
k<l\\
r<s\end{subarray}}W_{jm}(W_{ij}+W_{im})W_{vm}(W_{uv}+W_{um})W_{lm}(W_{kl}+W_{km})W_{sm}(W_{rs}+W_{rm}). $$

Taking expectations, we consider 4 types of cases in which the expectation is non-zero:

- • Case 1: $i=u=k=r$ and $j=v=l=s$ (1 instance),

- • Case 2: $i=k,u=r$ with $i\neq u$ and $j=l,v=s$ with $j\neq v$ (3 instances),

- • Case 3: $i=u=k=r$ and $j=l,v=s$ with $j\neq v$ (3 instances),

- • Case 4: $i=k,u=r$ with $i\neq u$ and $j=v=l=s$ (3 instances),

- • Other cases: $\mathbb{E}[W_{jm}(W_{ij}+W_{im})W_{vm}(W_{uv}+W_{um})W_{lm}(W_{kl}+W_{km})W_{sm}(W_{rs}+W_{rm}]=0$ .

It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[C_{n}^{4}X_{n,m}^{4}]= \displaystyle 16\biggl[\sum_{i<j}\mathbb{E}[W_{jm}^{4}]\mathbb{E}[(W_{ij}+W_{im})^{4}] \displaystyle+3\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i<j,u<v\\
i\neq u,j\neq v\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}[W_{jm}^{2}]\,\mathbb{E}[(W_{ij}+W_{im})^{2}]\,\mathbb{E}[W_{vm}^{2}]\,\mathbb{E}[(W_{ij}+W_{im})^{2}] \displaystyle+3\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i<j,v\\
j\neq v\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}[W_{jm}^{2}]\,\mathbb{E}[W_{vm}^{2}]\,\mathbb{E}[(W_{ij}+W_{im})^{2}(W_{iv}+W_{im})^{2}] \displaystyle+3\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i,u<j\\
i\neq u\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}[(W_{ij}+W_{im})^{2}]\,\mathbb{E}[(W_{uj}+W_{um})^{2}]\,\mathbb{E}[W_{jm}^{4}]\biggr]. $$

We provide upper bounds for the above expectations. Indeed for all $(a,b)\in\llbracket 1,n\rrbracket^{2}$

$$ \mathbb{E}[W_{ab}^{4}]=(1-\alpha_{n})^{4}\alpha_{n}+\alpha_{n}^{4}(1-\alpha_{n})=\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})(\alpha_{n}^{3}+(1-\alpha_{n})^{3}). $$

It is then straightforward to show, taking $c_{*}>0$ to be a high enough constant, that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[W_{jm}^{4}]\leq c_{*}\alpha_{n},\qquad\mathbb{E}[(W_{ij}+W_{im})^{4}]\leq c_{*}\alpha_{n},\qquad\mathbb{E}[W_{jm}^{2}]^{2}\leq c_{*}\alpha_{n}^{2}, \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[(W_{ij}+W_{im})^{2}]^{2}\leq c_{*}\alpha_{n}^{2},\qquad\mathbb{E}[(W_{ij}+W_{im})^{2}(W_{iv}+W_{im})^{2}]\leq c_{*}\alpha_{n}. $$

It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[C_{n}^{4}X_{n,m}^{4}] \displaystyle\leq 16\left(\sum_{i<j}c_{*}^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}+3\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i<j,u<v\\
i\neq u,j\neq v\end{subarray}}c_{*}^{2}\alpha_{n}^{4}+3\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i<j,v\\
j\neq v\end{subarray}}c_{*}^{2}\alpha_{n}^{3}+3\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i,u<j\\
i\neq u\end{subarray}}c_{*}^{2}\alpha_{n}^{3}\right) \displaystyle\leq 16c_{*}^{2}n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}\left(1+3n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}+6n\alpha_{n}\right) \displaystyle=O(n^{4}\alpha_{n}^{4}), $$

where in the last line we have used the assumption of $n\alpha_{n}\to\infty$ to identify the dominating term. Note that $C_{n}$ is at the order of $n\sqrt{n}\alpha_{n}$ . We thus obtain

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{4}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right] \displaystyle=n\cdot O\left(\frac{n^{4}\alpha_{n}^{4}}{(n\sqrt{n}\alpha_{n})^{4}}\right)=O\left(n^{-1}\right). $$

This proves (D.22).

### D.2 Proof of the null distribution of $\psi_{n}^{SQ}$

We aim to show that

$$ \varphi_{n}^{SQ}=\frac{Q_{n}}{2\sqrt{2}n^{2}\hat{\alpha}_{n}^{2}}\quad\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{\mathcal{L}}\quad\mathcal{N}(0,1). $$

Let $\hat{\delta}_{n}=\alpha_{n}-\hat{\alpha}_{n}$ . We then have $A_{ij}-\hat{\alpha}_{n}=W_{ij}+\hat{\delta}_{n}$ . It follows that $Q_{n}=\sum_{(i_{1},i_{2},i_{3},i_{4})\text{ dist.}}(W_{i_{1}i_{2}}+\hat{\delta}_{n})(W_{i_{2}i_{3}}+\hat{\delta}_{n})(W_{i_{3}i_{4}}+\hat{\delta}_{n})(W_{i_{4}i_{1}}+\hat{\delta}_{n})$ . We introduce an ideal version of $Q_{n}$ ,

$$ \tilde{Q}_{n}=\sum_{(i_{1},i_{2},i_{3},i_{4})\text{ dist.}}W_{i_{1}i_{2}}W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}W_{i_{4}i_{1}}, $$

and re-express

$$ \psi_{n}^{SQ}=\frac{Q_{n}}{2\sqrt{2}n^{2}\hat{\alpha}_{n}^{2}}=\frac{Q_{n}-\tilde{Q}_{n}}{2\sqrt{2}n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\left(\frac{\alpha_{n}}{\hat{\alpha}_{n}}\right)^{2}+\frac{\tilde{Q}_{n}}{2\sqrt{2}n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\left(\frac{\alpha_{n}}{\hat{\alpha}_{n}}\right)^{2}. $$

If we can show that

$$ \displaystyle\frac{Q_{n}-\tilde{Q}_{n}}{2\sqrt{2}n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0, \displaystyle\frac{\tilde{Q}_{n}}{2\sqrt{2}n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\rightarrow_{d}\mathcal{N}(0,1), $$

then (D.26) follows from Slutsky’s theorem and the fact that $\hat{\alpha}_{n}/\alpha_{n}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}1$ .

What remains is to prove (D.28) and (D.29).

Proof of Equation (D.28): Expanding $Q_{n}$ , we obtain:

$$ \displaystyle Q_{n}-\tilde{Q}_{n}= \displaystyle n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)\hat{\delta}_{n}^{4}+4(n-2)(n-3)\hat{\delta}_{n}^{3}\sum_{i\neq j}W_{ij} \displaystyle+4(n-3)\hat{\delta}_{n}^{2}\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}W_{ij}W_{jk}+2\hat{\delta}_{n}^{2}\sum_{i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}}W_{ij}W_{kl} \displaystyle+4\hat{\delta}_{n}\sum_{i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}}W_{ij}W_{jk}W_{kl}. $$

It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\biggl|\frac{Q_{n}-\tilde{Q}_{n}}{n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\biggr|\leq \displaystyle n^{2}\frac{\hat{\delta}_{n}^{4}}{\alpha_{n}^{2}}+4\frac{|\hat{\delta}_{n}|^{3}}{\alpha_{n}^{2}}\biggl|\sum_{i\neq j}W_{ij}\biggr|+\frac{4|\hat{\delta}_{n}|}{n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\biggl|\sum_{i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}}W_{ij}W_{jk}W_{kl}\biggr| \displaystyle+\frac{\hat{\delta}_{n}^{2}}{\alpha_{n}^{2}}\left(\frac{4}{n}\biggl|\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}W_{ij}W_{jk}\biggr|+\frac{2}{n^{2}}\biggl|\sum_{i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}}W_{ij}W_{kl}\biggr|\right). $$

We will bound each of the terms on the right hand side of (D.30).

Consider the first term in (D.30). Note that

$$ n^{2}\frac{\hat{\delta}_{n}^{4}}{\alpha_{n}^{2}}=4\frac{(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}}{(n-1)^{2}}\left(\sqrt{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}}\frac{\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\alpha_{n}}{\sqrt{\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}\right)^{4}. $$

By Central Limit Theorem, $\sqrt{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}}\frac{\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\alpha_{n}}{\sqrt{\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}\rightarrow\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ . It follows from Slutsky’s theorem that

$$ n^{2}\hat{\delta}_{n}^{4}/\alpha_{n}^{2}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0. $$

Consider the second term in (D.30). Since $\hat{\delta}_{n}=\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\alpha_{n}$ , using the definition of $\hat{\alpha}_{n}$ , we immediately have $\sum_{i<j}W_{ij}=\frac{n(n-1)}{2}\hat{\delta}_{n}$ . As a result,

$$ \frac{|\hat{\delta}_{n}^{3}|}{\alpha_{n}^{2}}\biggl|\sum_{i\neq j}W_{ij}\biggr|=n(n-1)\frac{\hat{\delta}_{n}^{4}}{\alpha_{n}^{2}}\leq n^{2}\frac{\hat{\delta}_{n}^{4}}{\alpha_{n}^{2}}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0. $$

Consider the fourth term in (D.30). First, let $A_{n}=\frac{1}{n^{3}\alpha_{n}}\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}W_{ij}W_{ik}$ . Applying Chebyshev’s inequality, we have that for any $\lambda>0$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{P}(|A_{n}|>\lambda) \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mathbb{E}[A_{n}^{2}]}{\lambda^{2}}\leq\frac{6^{2}}{n^{6}\alpha_{n}^{2}\lambda^{2}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i<j<k\\
u<v<w\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}[W_{ij}W_{jk}W_{uv}W_{vw}] \displaystyle=\frac{36}{n^{6}\alpha_{n}^{2}\lambda^{2}}\sum_{i<j<k}\mathbb{E}[W_{ij}^{2}W_{jk}^{2}]\leq\frac{36}{n^{3}\lambda^{2}}\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0, $$

which shows that $A_{n}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0$ . Furthermore,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\hat{\delta}_{n}^{2}}{n\alpha_{n}^{2}}\biggl|\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}W_{ij}W_{jk}\biggr| \displaystyle=2(1-\alpha_{n})\Bigl(\frac{n}{n-1}\Bigr)\biggl[\sqrt{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}}\frac{\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\alpha_{n}}{\sqrt{\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}\biggr]^{2}|A_{n}|. $$

By Slutsky’s theorem, we have

$$ \frac{\hat{\delta}_{n}^{2}}{n\alpha_{n}^{2}}\biggl|\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}W_{ij}W_{jk}\biggr|\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0. $$

Second, let $B_{n}=\frac{1}{\alpha_{n}n^{4}}\sum_{i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}}W_{ij}W_{kl}$ . We apply Chebyshev’s inequality: For any $\lambda>0$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{P}(|B_{n}|>\lambda) \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mathbb{E}[B_{n}^{2}]}{\lambda^{2}}\leq\frac{1}{\alpha_{n}^{2}n^{8}\lambda^{2}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}\\
s,t,u,v\text{ dist.}\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}[W_{ij}W_{kl}W_{st}W_{uv}] \displaystyle=\frac{24^{2}}{\alpha_{n}^{2}n^{8}\lambda^{2}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i<j<k<l\\
s<t<u<v\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}[W_{ij}W_{kl}W_{st}W_{uv}]=\frac{24^{2}}{\alpha_{n}^{2}n^{8}\lambda^{2}}\sum_{i<j<k<l}\mathbb{E}[W_{ij}^{2}W_{kl}^{2}] \displaystyle=\frac{24^{2}}{\alpha_{n}^{2}n^{8}\lambda^{2}}\sum_{i<j<k<l}\mathbb{E}[W_{ij}^{2}]\mathbb{E}[W_{kl}^{2}]\leq\frac{24^{2}}{n^{4}\lambda^{2}}\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0, $$

which shows that $B_{n}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0$ . Furthermore,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\hat{\delta}_{n}^{2}}{n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\biggl|\sum_{i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}}W_{ij}W_{kl}\biggr| \displaystyle=\frac{2(1-\alpha_{n})n}{n-1}\biggl[\sqrt{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}}\frac{\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\alpha_{n}}{\sqrt{\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}\biggr]^{2}|B_{n}|. $$

We conclude by Slutsky’s theorem that

$$ \frac{\hat{\delta}_{n}^{2}}{n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\biggl|\sum_{i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}}W_{ij}W_{kl}\biggr|\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0. $$

Consider the third term in (D.30). Write $D_{n}=\frac{1}{\alpha_{n}^{3/2}n^{3}}\sum_{i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}}W_{ij}W_{jk}W_{kl}$ . By Chebyshev’s inequality, for any $\lambda>0$ ,

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{P}(|D_{n}|>\lambda) \displaystyle\leq\frac{\mathbb{E}[D_{n}^{2}]}{\lambda^{2}}=\frac{1}{\alpha_{n}^{3}n^{6}\lambda^{2}}\mathbb{E}\Biggl[\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}\\
u,v,w,z\text{ dist.}\end{subarray}}W_{ij}W_{jk}W_{kl}W_{uv}W_{vw}W_{wz}\Biggr] \displaystyle=\frac{2}{\alpha_{n}^{3}n^{6}\lambda^{2}}\mathbb{E}\Biggl[\sum_{i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}}W_{ij}^{2}W_{jk}^{2}W_{kl}^{2}\Biggr]\leq\frac{2}{n^{2}\lambda^{2}}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}0, $$

which implies that $D_{n}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0$ . Furthermore,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\hat{\delta}_{n}}{n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\biggl|\sum_{i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}}W_{ij}W_{jk}W_{kl}\biggr| \displaystyle=\sqrt{\frac{2n(1-\alpha_{n})}{n-1}}\biggl[\sqrt{\frac{n(n-1)}{2}}\frac{\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\alpha_{n}}{\sqrt{\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}\biggr]|D_{n}|. $$

We conclude by Slutsky’s theorem that

$$ \frac{\hat{\delta}_{n}}{n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\left|\sum_{i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}}W_{ij}W_{jk}W_{kl}\right|\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0. $$

We plug (D.32)-(D.36) into (D.30) to get (D.28).

Proof of Equation (D.29): We introduce some notation to simplify the computations. Given 4 distinct nodes, there are 3 different possible cycles, denoted as

$$ CC(i_{1},i_{2},i_{3},i_{4})=\{(i_{1},i_{2},i_{3},i_{4}),(i_{1},i_{2},i_{4},i_{3}),(i_{1},i_{3},i_{2},i_{4})\}. $$

Moreover, for $B\subset\{1,2,...,n\}^{4}$ , let $CC(B)=\cup_{(i_{1},i_{2},i_{3},i_{4})\in B}CC(i_{1},i_{2},i_{3},i_{4})$ . For $1\leq m\leq n$ , let $I_{m}$ be the collection of $(i_{1},i_{2},i_{3},i_{4})$ such that $1\leq i_{1}<i_{2}<i_{3}<i_{4}\leq m$ . We thus have

$$ \tilde{Q}_{n}=8\sum_{CC(I_{n})}W_{i_{1}i_{2}}W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}W_{i_{4}i_{1}}. $$

It is straightforward to see that $\mathbb{E}[\tilde{Q}_{n}]=0$ . In addition, notice that the terms in the sum are uncorrelated, since they all correspond to different cycles: to obtain a non-zero correlation between $W_{i_{1}i_{2}}W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}W_{i_{4}i_{1}}$ and $W_{i_{1}^{\prime}i_{2}^{\prime}}W_{i_{2}^{\prime}i_{3}^{\prime}}W_{i_{3}^{\prime}i_{4}^{\prime}}W_{i_{4}^{\prime}i_{1}^{\prime}}$ , we would need to uniquely match each factor in $W_{i_{1}i_{2}}W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}W_{i_{4}i_{1}}$ with a factor in $W_{i_{1}^{\prime}i_{2}^{\prime}}W_{i_{2}^{\prime}i_{3}^{\prime}}W_{i_{3}^{\prime}i_{4}^{\prime}}W_{i_{4}^{\prime}i_{1}^{\prime}}$ , which is equivalent to overlaying the two cycles $[i_{1}i_{2}i_{3}i_{4}]$ and $[i^{\prime}_{1}i_{2}^{\prime}i_{3}^{\prime}i_{4}^{\prime}]$ . Let’s compute the variance

$$ \displaystyle\text{Var}(\tilde{Q}_{n}) \displaystyle=64\text{Var}\left(\sum_{CC(I_{n})}W_{i_{1}i_{2}}W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}W_{i_{4}i_{1}}\right) \displaystyle=64\alpha_{n}^{4}(1-\alpha_{n})^{4}\times 3{n\choose 4}=8\alpha_{n}^{4}(1-\alpha_{n})^{4}n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3). $$

Let $Z_{n}:=2\sqrt{2n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)}\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}$ . It is easy to see that $n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}/Z_{n}\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}1$ . By Slutsky’s theorem, to show (D.29), it suffices to show that

$$ \frac{\tilde{Q}_{n}}{Z_{n}}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{\mathcal{L}}\mathcal{N}(0,1). $$

We now prove (D.38). For each $1\leq m\leq n$ , we define

$$ X_{n,m}=\frac{\tilde{Q}_{n,m}-\tilde{Q}_{n,m-1}}{Z_{n}},\qquad\mbox{where}\quad\tilde{Q}_{n,m}=\sum_{CC(I_{m})}W_{i_{1}i_{2}}W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}W_{i_{4}i_{1}}. $$

By default, we let $\tilde{Q}_{n,0}=1$ . Recall that we previously defined the filtration $\{\mathcal{F}_{n,m}:0\leq m\leq n\}$ such that $\mathcal{F}_{n,m}=\sigma\{W_{ij}:(i,j)\in\llbracket 1,m\rrbracket^{2}\}$ for $m\geq 1$ and $\mathcal{F}_{n,0}=\{\Omega,\emptyset\}$ (where $\Omega$ denotes the sample space). It is easy to see that $\mathbb{E}[|\tilde{Q}_{n,m}|]<\infty$ . Hence, $\tilde{Q}_{n,m}$ is $\mathcal{F}_{n,m}$ -measurable. It is also straightforward to show that $\mathbb{E}[\tilde{Q}_{n,m+1}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m}]=\tilde{Q}_{n,m}$ . Therefore, the sequence $\{Q_{n,m}:m\in\llbracket 1,n\rrbracket\}$ is a martingale with respect to $\{\mathcal{F}_{n,m}:m\in\llbracket 1,n\rrbracket\}$ . It follows that the sequence $\{X_{n,m}:m\in\llbracket 1,n\rrbracket\}$ is a martingale difference sequence. Note that

$$ \tilde{Q}_{n}/Z_{n}=\tilde{Q}_{n,n}/Z_{n}=\sum_{m=1}^{n}X_{n,m}. $$

By the martingale Central Limit Theorem, to show (D.38), it suffices to show:

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}1, \displaystyle\forall\epsilon>0,\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}\bm{1}\{|X_{n,m}>\epsilon|\}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0. $$

Below, we show (D.39) and (D.40) separately.

In the first part, we prove (D.39). It suffices to show:

$$ \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right]=1, $$

and

$$ \text{Var}\left(\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right)\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0. $$

Consider (D.41) first. Recall that by definition

$$ X_{n,m}=\frac{\tilde{Q}_{n,m}-\tilde{Q}_{n,m-1}}{Z_{n}}=\frac{8}{Z_{n}}\sum_{CC(I_{m})\setminus CC(I_{m-1})}W_{i_{1}i_{2}}W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}W_{i_{4}i_{1}}. $$

An alternative way to enumerate all cycles in $CC(I_{m})\setminus CC(I_{m-1})$ is to first select a set of two indices $\{i,j\}$ (we take, wlog, $i<j$ ) from $\{1,...,m-1\}$ and use them as the neighboring nodes of $m$ in the cycle. Then select $k\in\{1,...,m-1\}\setminus\{i,j\}$ as the last node of the cycle.

$$ X_{n,m}=\frac{8}{Z_{n}}\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq m-1}W_{mi}W_{mj}Y_{m-1,ij},\qquad\mbox{where}\quad Y_{m-1,ij}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq k\leq m-1\\
k\notin\{i,j\}\end{subarray}}W_{ki}W_{kj}. $$

It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}] \displaystyle=\frac{64}{Z_{n}^{2}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i<j\leq m-1\\
1\leq u<v\leq m-1\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}[W_{mi}W_{mj}Y_{m-1,ij}W_{mu}W_{mv}Y_{m-1,uv}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}] \displaystyle=\frac{64}{Z_{n}^{2}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i<j\leq m-1\\
1\leq u<v\leq m-1\end{subarray}}Y_{m-1,ij}Y_{m-1,uv}\mathbb{E}[W_{mi}W_{mj}W_{mu}W_{mv}] \displaystyle=\frac{64}{Z_{n}^{2}}\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq m-1}Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}\mathbb{E}[W_{mi}^{2}W_{mj}^{2}]=\frac{64\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}}{Z_{n}^{2}}\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq m-1}Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}. $$

Hence

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right] \displaystyle=\frac{64\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}}{Z_{n}^{2}}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq m-1}\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}], $$

where

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}] \displaystyle=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq k,l\leq m-1\\
k,l\notin\{i,j\}\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}\left[W_{ki}W_{kj}W_{li}W_{lj}\right]=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq k\leq m-1\\
k\notin\{i,j\}\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}\left[W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2}\right] \displaystyle=(m-3)\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}. $$

It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right] \displaystyle=\frac{64\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}}{Z_{n}^{2}}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\frac{(m-1)(m-2)(m-3)}{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}=1. $$

This proves (D.41).

Consider (D.42) next. We decompose $\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]$ into a sum of two components, then calculate its variance. Note that

$$ Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}=\Biggl(\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq k\leq m-1\\
k\notin\{i,j\}\end{subarray}}W_{ki}W_{kj}\Biggr)^{2}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq k\leq m-1\\
k\notin\{i,j\}\end{subarray}}W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2}+2\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq k<l\leq m-1\\
k,l\notin\{i,j\}\end{subarray}}W_{ki}W_{kj}W_{li}W_{lj}. $$

Hence

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}] \displaystyle=\frac{64\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}}{Z_{n}^{2}}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq m-1}Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}=\frac{16n^{4}\alpha_{n}^{4}}{Z_{n}^{2}}(I_{a}+I_{b}), $$

where we denote

$$ \displaystyle I_{a} \displaystyle=\frac{4(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}}{n^{4}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq m-1}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq k\leq m-1\\
k\notin\{i,j\}\end{subarray}}W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2}, \displaystyle I_{b} \displaystyle=\frac{8(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}}{n^{4}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq m-1}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq k<l\leq m-1\\
k,l\notin\{i,j\}\end{subarray}}W_{ki}W_{kj}W_{li}W_{lj}. $$

Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality we obtain

$$ \displaystyle\text{Var}\left(\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right) \displaystyle=\frac{256n^{8}\alpha_{n}^{8}}{Z_{n}^{4}}(\text{Var}(I_{a})+\text{Var}(I_{b})+2\text{Cov}(I_{a},I_{b})) \displaystyle\leq\frac{256n^{8}\alpha_{n}^{8}}{Z_{n}^{4}}(\sqrt{\text{Var}(I_{a})}+\sqrt{\text{Var}(I_{b})})^{2}. $$

Hence, it suffices to show that $\text{Var}(I_{a})\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0$ and $\text{Var}(I_{b})\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0$ separately. For $\text{Var}(I_{a})$ , we first rearrange the sums in the expression of $I_{a}$

$$ \displaystyle I_{a} \displaystyle=\frac{4(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}}{n^{4}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i<j\leq n-1\\
i,j\neq k\end{subarray}}\sum_{m>\max\{i,j,k\}}W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2} \displaystyle=\frac{4(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}}{n^{4}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i<j\leq n-1\\
i,j\neq k\end{subarray}}(n-\max\{i,j,k\}+1)W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2}. $$

Note that the terms of the first sum over $k=1,...,n$ are pairwise independent, which will facilitate variance computations. Hence

$$ \displaystyle\text{Var}(I_{a}) \displaystyle=\frac{16(1-\alpha_{n})^{4}}{n^{8}\alpha_{n}^{4}}\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\text{Var}\left(\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i<j\leq n-1\\
i,j\neq k\end{subarray}}(n-\max\{i,j,k\}+1)W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2}\right) \displaystyle\leq\frac{16(1-\alpha_{n})^{4}}{n^{6}\alpha_{n}^{4}}\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i<j\leq n-1\\
i,j\neq k\end{subarray}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq u<v\leq n-1\\
u,v\neq k\end{subarray}}\text{Cov}(W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2},W_{ku}^{2}W_{kv}^{2}). $$

We can consider four cases for $\text{Cov}(W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2},W_{ku}^{2}W_{kv}^{2})$ :

- 1. $(i,j)=(u,v)$ , then $\text{Var}(W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2})\leq\mathbb{E}[W_{ki}^{4}W_{kj}^{4}]=\mathbb{E}[W_{ki}^{4}]^{2}\leq c\alpha_{n}^{2}$ ,

- 2. $i=u,j\neq v$ , then $\text{Cov}(W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2},W_{ki}^{2}W_{kv}^{2})\leq\mathbb{E}[W_{ki}^{4}W_{kj}^{2}W_{kv}^{2}]=\mathbb{E}[W_{ki}^{4}]\mathbb{E}[W_{kj}^{2}]^{2}\leq c\alpha_{n}^{3}$ ,

- 3. The previous bound will also hold for the case $i\neq u,j=v$ , the case $i=v$ , and the case $j=u$ ,

- 4. For any other case, $\text{Cov}(W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2},W_{ki}^{2}W_{kv}^{2})=0$ .

Here, $c>0$ is a high enough constant. It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\text{Var}(I_{a}) \displaystyle=\frac{16(1-\alpha_{n})^{4}}{n^{8}\alpha_{n}^{4}}\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i<j\leq n-1\\
i,j\neq k\end{subarray}}\left\{\text{Var}(W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2})+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v=i+1\\
v\notin\{k,j\}\end{subarray}}^{n-1}\text{Cov}(W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2},W_{ki}^{2}W_{kv}^{2})\right. \displaystyle+\left.\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}u=1\\
u\notin\{k,i\}\end{subarray}}^{j-1}\text{Cov}(W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2},W_{ku}^{2}W_{kj}^{2})+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}u=1\\
u\neq k\end{subarray}}^{i-1}\text{Cov}(W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2},W_{ku}^{2}W_{ki}^{2})+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}v=j+1\\
v\neq k\end{subarray}}^{n-1}\text{Cov}(W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2},W_{kj}^{2}W_{kv}^{2})\right\} \displaystyle\leq\frac{16c(1-\alpha_{n})^{4}}{n^{8}\alpha_{n}^{4}}\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i<j\leq n-1\\
i,j\neq k\end{subarray}}\left\{\alpha_{n}^{2}+4n\alpha_{n}^{3}\right\}\leq\frac{8c}{n^{3}(n\alpha_{n})}\left(4+\frac{1}{n\alpha_{n}}\right)\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0. $$

Let’s now show that $\text{Var}(I_{b})\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0$ . Recall that

$$ \displaystyle I_{b} \displaystyle=\frac{8(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}}{n^{4}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq m-1}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq k<l\leq m-1\\
k,l\notin\{i,j\}\end{subarray}}W_{ki}W_{kj}W_{li}W_{lj} \displaystyle=\frac{2(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}}{n^{4}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i,j,k,l\leq m-1\\
i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}\end{subarray}}W_{ki}W_{kj}W_{li}W_{lj} \displaystyle=\frac{2(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}}{n^{4}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i,j,k,l\leq n-1\\
i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}\end{subarray}}\sum_{m>\max\{i,j,k,l\}}W_{ki}W_{kj}W_{li}W_{lj} \displaystyle=\frac{2(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}}{n^{4}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i,j,k,l\leq n-1\\
i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}\end{subarray}}(n+1-\max\{i,j,k,l\})W_{ki}W_{kj}W_{li}W_{lj}. $$

Therefore,

$$ \displaystyle\text{Var}(I_{b}) \displaystyle=\frac{4(1-\alpha_{n})^{4}}{n^{8}\alpha_{n}^{4}}\text{Var}\left(\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i,j,k,l\leq n-1\\
i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}\end{subarray}}(n+1-\max\{i,j,k,l\})W_{ik}W_{kj}W_{jl}W_{li}\right) \displaystyle=\frac{4(1-\alpha_{n})^{4}}{n^{8}\alpha_{n}^{4}}\text{Var}\left(8\sum_{CC(I_{n-1})}(n+1-\max\{i,j,k,l\})W_{ik}W_{kj}W_{jl}W_{li}\right) \displaystyle=\frac{32(1-\alpha_{n})^{4}}{n^{8}\alpha_{n}^{4}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i,j,k,l\leq n-1\\
i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}\end{subarray}}(n+1-\max\{i,j,k,l\})^{2}\text{Var}(W_{ik}W_{kj}W_{jl}W_{li}) \displaystyle\leq\frac{32(1-\alpha_{n})^{4}}{n^{6}\alpha_{n}^{4}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i,j,k,l\leq n-1\\
i,j,k,l\text{ dist.}\end{subarray}}\alpha_{n}^{4}(1-\alpha_{n})^{4}\leq\frac{32}{n^{2}}\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0. $$

This gives $\text{Var}(I_{b})\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0$ . Recall that we had:

$$ \text{Var}\left(\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right)\leq\frac{256n^{8}\alpha_{n}^{8}}{Z_{n}^{4}}\left(\sqrt{\text{Var}(I_{a})}+\sqrt{\text{Var}(I_{b})}\right)^{2}. $$

Since $\frac{256n^{8}\alpha_{n}^{8}}{Z_{n}^{4}}\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}4$ , we obtain (D.42). In combination with (D.41), this proves (D.39).

In the second part, we prove (D.40). We have, using the Cauchy-Schwarz and Markov inequalities

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{2}\bm{1}\{|X_{n,m}>\epsilon|\}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}] \displaystyle\leq\sum_{m=1}^{n}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{4}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]}\sqrt{\mathbb{P}(|X_{n,m}|\geq\epsilon|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}])} \displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{\epsilon^{2}}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{4}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]. $$

Hence it suffices to show that

$$ \mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{4}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\right]=\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{4}]\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0. $$

Recall that for all $n\in\mathbb{N}^{*}$ , for all $m\in\llbracket 1,n\rrbracket$

$$ X_{n,m}=\frac{2}{Z_{n}}\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq m-1}W_{mi}W_{mj}Y_{m-1,ij}\quad\text{ with }\quad Y_{m-1,ij}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq k\leq m-1\\
k\notin\{i,j\}\end{subarray}}W_{ki}W_{kj}. $$

It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{4}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{16}{Z_{n}^{4}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i<j,u<v\\
k<l,r<s\end{subarray}}Y_{m-1,ij}Y_{m-1,uv}Y_{m-1,kl}Y_{m-1,rs}\times\mathbb{E}[W_{mi}W_{mj}W_{mu}W_{mv}W_{mk}W_{ml}W_{mr}W_{ms}] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{16}{Z_{n}^{4}}\left\{\sum_{i<j}Y_{m-1,ij}^{4}\mathbb{E}[W_{mi}^{4}W_{mj}^{4}]+3\sum_{i}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}j,v\\
j,v>i\text{ and }j\neq v\end{subarray}}Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}Y_{m-1,iv}^{2}\mathbb{E}[W_{mi}^{4}W_{mj}^{2}W_{mv}^{2}]\right. \displaystyle\left.+3\sum_{j}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i,u\\
i,u<j\text{ and }i\neq u\end{subarray}}Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}Y_{m-1,uj}^{2}\mathbb{E}[W_{mj}^{4}W_{mi}^{2}W_{mu}^{2}]+9\sum_{i<j,u<v}Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}Y_{m-1,uv}^{2}\mathbb{E}[W_{mi}^{2}W_{mj}^{2}W_{mu}^{2}W_{mv}^{2}]\right\} \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\frac{16}{Z_{n}^{4}}\left\{\sum_{i<j}Y_{m-1,ij}^{4}c\alpha_{n}^{2}+3\sum_{i}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}j,v\\
j,v>i\text{ and }j\neq v\end{subarray}}Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}Y_{m-1,iv}^{2}c\alpha_{n}^{3}\right. \displaystyle\left.+3\sum_{j}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i,u\\
i,u<j\text{ and }i\neq u\end{subarray}}Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}Y_{m-1,uj}^{2}c\alpha_{n}^{3}+9\sum_{i<j,u<v}Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}Y_{m-1,uv}^{2}c\alpha_{n}^{4}\right\}, $$

where $c>0$ is a high enough constant. Hence,

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{4}] \displaystyle\leq\frac{16c}{Z_{n}^{4}}\left\{\alpha_{n}^{2}\sum_{i<j}\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,ij}^{4}]+3\alpha_{n}^{3}\sum_{i}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}j,v\\
j,v>i\text{ and }j\neq v\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}Y_{m-1,iv}^{2}]\right. \displaystyle\left.+3\alpha_{n}^{3}\sum_{j}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i,u\\
i,u<j\text{ and }i\neq u\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}Y_{m-1,uj}^{2}]+9\alpha_{n}^{4}\sum_{i<j,u<v}\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}]\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,uv}^{2}]\right\}. $$

We will now compute upper bounds on $\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,ij}^{4}]$ , $\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}Y_{m-1,iv}^{2}]$ and $\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}]$ . We have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,ij}^{4}] \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{k,l,u,v\notin\{i,j\}}W_{ki}W_{kj}W_{li}W_{lj}W_{ui}W_{uj}W_{vi}W_{vj}\right] \displaystyle=3\sum_{k,u\notin\{i,j\}}\mathbb{E}[W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2}W_{ui}^{2}W_{uj}^{2}] \displaystyle=3\left(\sum_{k\notin\{i,j\}}\mathbb{E}[W_{ki}^{4}W_{kj}^{4}]+\sum_{k\neq u;\;k,u\notin\{i,j\}}\mathbb{E}[W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2}W_{ui}^{2}W_{uj}^{2}]\right) \displaystyle\leq 12m\alpha_{n}^{2}+3m^{2}\alpha_{n}^{4}\leq c_{1}(m\alpha_{n}^{2}+m^{2}\alpha_{n}^{4}), $$

where $c_{1}>0$ is a constant. Similarly

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}] \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{k,l\notin\{i,j\}}W_{ki}W_{kj}W_{li}W_{lj}\right]=\sum_{k\notin\{i,j\}}\mathbb{E}[W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2}]\leq m\alpha_{n}^{2}, $$

and

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E} \displaystyle[Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}Y_{m-1,iv}^{2}]=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{k,l,r,s:k,l\notin\{i,j\},r,s\notin\{i,v\}}W_{ki}W_{kj}W_{li}W_{lj}W_{ri}W_{rv}W_{si}W_{sv}\right] \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{k,r:k\notin\{i,j\},r\notin\{i,v\}}W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2}W_{ri}^{2}W_{rv}^{2}\right]=\sum_{k,r:k\notin\{i,j\},r\notin\{i,v\}}\mathbb{E}[W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2}W_{ri}^{2}W_{rv}^{2}] \displaystyle=\sum_{k\notin\{i,j,v\}}\mathbb{E}[W_{ki}^{4}W_{kj}^{2}W_{kv}^{2}]+\sum_{k\neq r;k\notin\{i,j\},r\notin\{i,v\}}\mathbb{E}[W_{ki}^{2}W_{kj}^{2}W_{ri}^{2}W_{rv}^{2}] \displaystyle\leq 2m\alpha_{n}^{3}+m^{2}\alpha_{n}^{4}\leq c_{2}m^{2}\alpha_{n}^{3}, $$

for $n$ big enough (since $\alpha_{n}\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0$ ), where $c_{2}>0$ is a constant. It follows that, for some constant $\gamma>\max\{1,c,c_{1},c_{2}\}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{4}] \displaystyle\leq\frac{16c}{Z_{n}^{4}}\left\{\alpha_{n}^{2}\sum_{i<j}\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,ij}^{4}]+3\alpha_{n}^{3}\sum_{i}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}j,v\\
j,v>i\text{ and }j\neq v\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}Y_{m-1,iv}^{2}]\right. \displaystyle\left.+3\alpha_{n}^{3}\sum_{j}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i,u\\
i,u<j\text{ and }i\neq u\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}Y_{m-1,uj}^{2}]+9\alpha_{n}^{4}\sum_{i<j,u<v}\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,ij}^{2}]\mathbb{E}[Y_{m-1,uv}^{2}]\right\} \displaystyle\leq\frac{16\gamma^{2}}{Z_{n}^{4}}(m^{3}\alpha_{n}^{4}+m^{4}\alpha_{n}^{6}+6m^{5}\alpha_{n}^{6}+9\alpha_{n}^{8}m^{6}) \displaystyle\leq\frac{16\gamma^{2}}{Z_{n}^{4}}(n^{3}\alpha_{n}^{4}+n^{4}\alpha_{n}^{6}+6n^{5}\alpha_{n}^{6}+9\alpha_{n}^{8}n^{6}). $$

As a result,

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[X_{n,m}^{4}] \displaystyle\leq\frac{16\gamma^{2}}{n^{2}(n-1)^{2}(n-2)^{2}(n-3)^{2}\alpha_{n}^{8}(1-\alpha_{n})^{8}}(n^{4}\alpha_{n}^{4}+n^{5}\alpha_{n}^{6}+6n^{6}\alpha_{n}^{6}+9\alpha_{n}^{8}n^{7}) \displaystyle=\left(\frac{144\gamma^{2}n^{6}}{(n-1)^{2}(n-2)^{2}(n-3)^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{8}}\right)\left(\frac{1}{n^{4}\alpha_{n}^{4}}+\frac{1}{n^{3}\alpha_{n}^{2}}+\frac{1}{n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}+\frac{1}{n}\right)\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}0. $$

This gives (D.43). Then, (D.40) follows immediately.

### D.3 Proof of the joint null distribution

We now show the desirable claim (D.1). We shall use the previously defined notations:

$$ \displaystyle T_{n} \displaystyle=\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}(A_{ik}-\alpha_{n})(A_{jk}-\alpha_{n}),\qquad\hat{T}_{n}=\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist.}}(A_{ik}-\hat{\alpha}_{n})(A_{jk}-\hat{\alpha}_{n}), \displaystyle\tilde{Q}_{n} \displaystyle=\sum_{(i_{1},i_{2},i_{3},i_{4})\text{ dist.}}W_{i_{1}i_{2}}W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}W_{i_{4}i_{1}}. $$

We have seen the decomposition of $\psi_{n}^{DC}$ in (D.3) and the decomposition of $\psi_{n}^{SQ}$ in (D.27). We plug them into the definition of $S_{n}$ to get:

$$ \displaystyle S_{n} \displaystyle=u\left[\frac{\hat{T}_{n}}{(n-1)\hat{\alpha}_{n}(1-\hat{\alpha}_{n})}\right]+v\left[\frac{Q_{n}-\tilde{Q}_{n}}{2\sqrt{2}n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\left(\frac{\alpha_{n}}{\hat{\alpha}_{n}}\right)^{2}+\frac{\tilde{Q}_{n}}{2\sqrt{2}n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\left(\frac{\alpha_{n}}{\hat{\alpha}_{n}}\right)^{2}\right] \displaystyle=\epsilon_{n}+u\frac{\frac{T_{n}}{(n-1)\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}{\sqrt{\frac{2n(n-2)}{(n-1)}}}+v\frac{\tilde{Q}_{n}}{2\sqrt{2}n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}, $$

where

$$ \epsilon_{n}=u\frac{\frac{T_{n}}{(n-1)\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}{\sqrt{\frac{2n(n-2)}{(n-1)}}}\left[\frac{\sqrt{n-1}\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})\hat{T}_{n}}{\sqrt{n-2}\hat{\alpha}_{n}(1-\hat{\alpha}_{n})T_{n}}-1\right]+v\left[\frac{\alpha^{2}_{n}}{\hat{\alpha}^{2}_{n}}\frac{(Q_{n}-\tilde{Q}_{n})}{2\sqrt{2}n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}+\Bigl(\frac{\alpha^{2}_{n}}{\hat{\alpha}^{2}_{n}}-1\Bigr)\frac{\tilde{Q}_{n}}{2\sqrt{2}n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\right]. $$

In Sections D.1-D.2, we have shown that

$$ \frac{\hat{\alpha}_{n}}{\alpha_{n}}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}1,\qquad\frac{\hat{T}_{n}}{T_{n}}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}1,\qquad\frac{\frac{T_{n}}{(n-1)\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}{\sqrt{\frac{2n(n-2)}{(n-1)}}}\xrightarrow{d}\mathcal{N}(0,1),\qquad\frac{Q_{n}-\tilde{Q}_{n}}{2\sqrt{2}n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\xrightarrow{d}\mathcal{N}(0,1). $$

It follows immediately that $\epsilon_{n}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0$ . By Slutsky’s theorem, it suffices to show that

$$ C_{n}\overset{\Delta}{=}u\frac{\frac{T_{n}}{(n-1)\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}{\sqrt{\frac{2n(n-2)}{(n-1)}}}+v\frac{\tilde{Q}_{n}}{2\sqrt{2}n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\quad\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{\mathcal{L}}\quad\mathcal{N}(0,1). $$

Below, we show (D.47). In Section D.1, we have defined $I_{m}$ as the collection of all distinct $\{(i,j,k)$ such that $1\leq i,j,k\leq m$ ; in Section D.2, we have defined $CC(I_{m})$ . For each $1\leq m\leq n$ , let

$$ T_{n,m}=\sum_{(j_{1},j_{2},j_{3})\in I_{m}}W_{j_{1}j_{3}}W_{j_{2}j_{3}},\qquad\tilde{Q}_{n,m}=\sum_{CC(I_{m})}W_{i_{1}i_{2}}W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}W_{i_{4}i_{1}}, $$

where $T_{n,0}=\tilde{Q}_{n,0}=0$ by default. Introduce

$$ C_{n,m}=u\frac{\frac{T_{n,m}}{(n-1)\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}{\sqrt{\frac{2n(n-2)}{(n-1)}}}+v\frac{\tilde{Q}_{n,m}}{2\sqrt{2}n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}},\qquad\mbox{for all }0\leq m\leq n. $$

We have seen that $\{T_{n,m}\}_{0\leq m\leq n}$ and $\{\tilde{Q}_{n,m}\}_{0\leq m\leq n}$ are both martingales with respect to the filtration $\{\mathcal{F}_{n,m}\}_{0\leq m\leq n}$ defined before. It is easy to see that $\{C_{n,m}\}_{0\leq m\leq n}$ is also a martingale. Write

$$ C_{n}=\sum_{m=1}^{n}D_{n,m},\qquad\mbox{where}\quad D_{n,m}\equiv C_{n,m}-C_{n,m-1}. $$

To show $C_{n}\xrightarrow{d}\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ , we apply the martingale Central Limit Theorem. It suffices to show:

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[D_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}1, \displaystyle\forall\epsilon>0,\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[D_{n,m}^{2}\bm{1}\{|D_{n,m}>\epsilon|\}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0. $$

It remains to show (D.48)-(D.49). Consider (D.49). Write

$$ D^{(1)}_{n,m}=\frac{\frac{T_{n,m}-T_{n,m-1}}{(n-1)\alpha_{n}(1-\alpha_{n})}}{\sqrt{\frac{2n(n-2)}{(n-1)}}},\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad D^{(1)}_{n,m}=\frac{\tilde{Q}_{n,m}-\tilde{Q}_{n,m-1}}{2\sqrt{2}n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{2}}. $$

Then, $D_{n,m}=uD^{(1)}_{n,m}+vD^{(2)}_{n,m}$ . It follows that $D^{4}_{n,m}\leq 8u^{4}(D^{(1)}_{n,m})^{4}+8v^{4}(D^{(2)}_{n,m})^{4}$ . As a result, for any $\epsilon>0$ , by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and the Markov inequality, we have

$$ \displaystyle\biggl(\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[D_{n,m}^{2}\bm{1}\{|D_{n,m} \displaystyle>\epsilon|\}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\biggr)^{2}\leq\biggl(\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[D_{n,m}^{4}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\biggr)\cdot\mathbb{P}\bigl(|D_{n,m}|>\epsilon|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}\bigr) \displaystyle\leq\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[D_{n,m}^{4}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}] \displaystyle\leq 8u^{4}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[(D^{(1)}_{n,m})^{4}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]+8v^{4}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[(D^{(2)}_{n,m})^{4}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]. $$

With significant efforts, we have shown $\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[(D^{(1)}_{n,m})^{4}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0$ in Section D.1, and we have shown $\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[(D^{(2)}_{n,m})^{4}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}$ in Section D.2. Plugging them into the above inequality, we immediately obtain (D.49).

Consider (D.48). Write

$$ \displaystyle A_{n}=\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[(D^{(1)}_{n,m})^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}],\qquad B_{n}=\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[(D^{(2)}_{n,m})^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}], \displaystyle M_{n}=\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[(D^{(1)}_{n,m})D^{(2)}_{n,m}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]. $$

Then,

$$ \sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[D_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]=u^{2}A_{n}+v^{2}B_{n}+2uvM_{n}, $$

In Sections D.1-D.2, we have shown that $A_{n}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}1$ and $B_{n}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}1$ . We claim that

$$ M_{n}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0. $$

Then, it follows that $\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[D_{n,m}^{2}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}u^{2}\cdot 1+v^{2}\cdot 1+2uv\cdot 0=1$ . This gives (D.48).

It remains to show (D.50). Using the expressions of $D^{(1)}_{n,m}$ and $D^{(2)}_{n,m}$ , we have

$$ M_{n}=\frac{\tilde{M}_{n}}{n^{2}\alpha_{n}^{3}(1-\alpha_{n})\sqrt{n(n-1)(n-2)}}, $$

where $\tilde{M}_{n}=\sum_{m=1}^{n}\mathbb{E}[(T_{n,m}-T_{n,m-1})(\tilde{Q}_{n,m}-\tilde{Q}_{n,m-1})|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]$ . We plug in the definitions of $T_{n,m}$ and $\tilde{Q}_{n,m}$ to get

$$ \tilde{M}_{n}=\sum_{m=1}^{n}\left(\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}(j_{1},j_{2},j_{3})\in\\
I_{m}\setminus I_{m-1}\end{subarray}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}(i_{1},i_{2},i_{3},i_{4})\in\\
CC(I_{m})\setminus CC(I_{m-1})\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}\left[W_{j_{1}j_{3}}W_{j_{2}j_{3}}\cdot W_{i_{1}i_{2}}W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}W_{i_{4}i_{1}}\middle|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}\right]\right). $$

Let’s see when $\mathbb{E}[W_{j_{1}j_{3}}W_{j_{2}j_{3}}W_{i_{1}i_{2}}W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}W_{i_{4}i_{1}}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]\neq 0$ . Since $(i_{1},i_{2},i_{3},i_{4})\in CC(I_{m})\setminus CC(I_{m-1})$ , exactly one of the four indices must be $m$ . We assume $i_{1}=m$ without loss of generality. Since $(j_{1},j_{2},j_{3})\in I_{m}\setminus I_{m-1}$ , exactly one of the three indices must be $m$ . Without loss of generality, we assume either $j_{1}=m$ or $j_{3}=m$ . If $j_{1}=m$ (and recall that we have assumed $i_{1}=m$ ), then

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[W_{j_{1}j_{3}}W_{j_{2}j_{3}}W_{i_{1}i_{2}}W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}W_{i_{4}i_{1}}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}] \displaystyle=\quad \displaystyle W_{j_{2}j_{3}}W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}\cdot\mathbb{E}[W_{mj_{3}}W_{mi_{2}}W_{i_{4}m}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]. $$

It is nonzero only if $j_{3}=i_{2}=i_{4}$ . However, this is impossible, because $i_{2}$ and $i_{4}$ need to be distinct. If $j_{3}=m$ (and recall that we have assumed $i_{1}=m$ ), we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[W_{j_{1}j_{3}}W_{j_{2}j_{3}}W_{i_{1}i_{2}}W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}W_{i_{4}i_{1}}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}] \displaystyle=\quad \displaystyle W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}\cdot\mathbb{E}[W_{j_{1}m}W_{j_{2}m}W_{mi_{2}}W_{i_{4}m}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}]. $$

Note that $j_{1}\neq j_{2}$ and $i_{2}\neq i_{4}$ . For the above to be nonzero, we must have $\{i_{2},i_{4}\}=\{j_{1},j_{2}\}$ . It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\tilde{M}_{n} \displaystyle=8\sum_{m=1}^{n}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i_{2},i_{3},i_{4}\leq m-1\\
\text{(distinct)}\end{subarray}}W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}\cdot\mathbb{E}[W^{2}_{mi_{2}}W^{2}_{mi_{4}}|\mathcal{F}_{n,m-1}] \displaystyle=8\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}\sum_{m=1}^{n}\sum_{(i_{2},i_{3},i_{4})\in I_{m-1}}W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}} \displaystyle=8\alpha_{n}^{2}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}\sum_{(i_{2},i_{3},i_{4})\in I_{n-1}}(n-\max\{i_{2},i_{3},i_{4}\})W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}. $$

As a result,

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[M_{n}^{2}] \displaystyle=\frac{\mathbb{E}[\tilde{M}^{2}_{n}]}{n^{5}(n-1)(n-2)\alpha_{n}^{6}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}} \displaystyle=\frac{64\alpha_{n}^{4}(1-\alpha_{n})^{4}}{n^{5}(n-1)(n-2)\alpha_{n}^{6}(1-\alpha_{n})^{2}}\times\mathbb{E}\left[\Biggl(\sum_{(i_{2},i_{3},i_{4})\in I_{n-1}}(n-\max\{i_{2},i_{3},i_{4}\})W_{i_{2}i_{3}}W_{i_{3}i_{4}}\Biggr)^{2}\right] \displaystyle\leq\frac{C}{n^{7}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\sum_{i_{2},i_{3},i_{4}}n^{2}\cdot\mathbb{E}[W^{2}_{i_{2}i_{3}}W^{2}_{i_{3}i_{4}}] \displaystyle\leq\frac{C}{n^{7}\alpha_{n}^{2}}\times n^{5}\alpha_{n}^{2}\quad\xrightarrow{n\to\infty}\quad 0. $$

Then, (D.50) follows directly. This completes the proof of Theorem 3.1. ∎

## Appendix E Proof of Theorem 3.2

Define

$$ U_{n}=\frac{\hat{\alpha}_{n}(1-\hat{\alpha}_{n})}{\alpha_{0}(1-\alpha_{0})}-1,\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad Z_{n}^{*}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(d_{i}-\bar{d})^{2}}{(n-1)\alpha_{0}(1-\alpha_{0})}-n. $$

By definition, $X_{n}=(1+U_{n})^{-1}(n+Z_{n}^{*})$ . It follows that

$$ \psi_{n}^{DC}\equiv\frac{X_{n}-n}{\sqrt{n}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}(1+U_{n})}(Z_{n}^{*}-nU_{n}). $$

The asymptotic behavior of $\psi_{n}^{DC}$ is mainly determined by $Z_{n}^{*}$ . Below, we first calculate the mean and variance of $Z_{n}^{*}$ ; then, we use these results to study the mean and variance of $\psi_{n}^{DC}$ .

The mean and variance of $Z_{n}^{*}$ . We introduce a matrix

$$ \tilde{\Omega}=\Omega-\alpha_{0}\bm{1}_{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime},\qquad\mbox{where}\quad\alpha_{0}=h^{\prime}Ph. $$

Then, $A_{ij}=W_{ij}+\tilde{\Omega}_{ij}+\alpha_{0}$ , for all $i\neq j$ . Write $\tilde{\Omega}^{*}=\tilde{\Omega}-\mathrm{diag}(\tilde{\Omega})$ . It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(d_{i}-\bar{d}\right)^{2}=\;\; \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(\sum_{j:j\neq i}(W_{ij}+\tilde{\Omega}_{ij}+\alpha_{0})-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{(k,\ell):k\neq\ell}(W_{k\ell}+\tilde{\Omega}_{k\ell}+\alpha_{0})\right)^{2} \displaystyle=\;\; \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(e_{i}^{\prime}W\bm{1}_{n}+e_{i}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}-\frac{1}{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}W\bm{1}_{n}-\frac{1}{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}\right)^{2} \displaystyle=\;\; \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(e_{i}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}-\frac{1}{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}\right)^{2}+2\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(e_{i}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}-\frac{1}{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}\right)(e_{i}^{\prime}W\bm{1}_{n}) \displaystyle-2\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(e_{i}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}-\frac{1}{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}\right)\left(\frac{1}{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}W\bm{1}_{n}\right)+\sum_{i=1}^{n}(e_{i}^{\prime}W\bm{1}_{n})^{2} \displaystyle+\frac{1}{n}(\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}W\bm{1}_{n})^{2}-2\sum_{i=1}^{n}(e_{i}^{\prime}W\bm{1}_{n})\left(\frac{1}{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}W\bm{1}_{n}\right) \displaystyle=\;\; \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(e_{i}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}-\frac{1}{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}\right)^{2}+2\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(e_{i}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}-\frac{1}{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}\right)(e_{i}^{\prime}W\bm{1}_{n}) \displaystyle+\sum_{i=1}^{n}(e_{i}^{\prime}W\bm{1}_{n})^{2}-\frac{1}{n}(\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}W\bm{1}_{n})^{2}. $$

We further combine the last two terms of (E.2):

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}(e_{i}^{\prime}W\bm{1}_{n})^{2}-\frac{1}{n}(\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}W\bm{1}_{n})^{2} \displaystyle=\;\; \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(\sum_{j:j\neq i}W_{ij}\right)^{2}-\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{i\neq j}W_{ij}\right)^{2} \displaystyle=\;\; \displaystyle\sum_{i\neq j}W_{ij}^{2}+\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist}}W_{ij}W_{ik}-\frac{2}{n}\sum_{i\neq j}W_{ij}^{2}-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i\neq j}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}k\neq l\\
\{k,l\}\neq\{i,j\}\end{subarray}}W_{ij}W_{kl} \displaystyle=\;\; \displaystyle\frac{n-2}{n}\sum_{i\neq j}W_{ij}^{2}+\sum_{i,j,k,\text{ dist}}W_{ij}W_{ik}-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i\neq j}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}k\neq l\\
\{k,l\}\neq\{i,j\}\end{subarray}}W_{ij}W_{kl}. $$

We plug it into (E.2) to get

$$ \displaystyle(n-1)\alpha_{0}(1-\alpha_{0})Z_{n}^{*} \displaystyle\equiv\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(d_{i}-\bar{d}\right)^{2}-n(n-1)\alpha_{0}(1-\alpha_{0}) \displaystyle=Y_{1}+2Y_{2}+Y_{3}+Y_{4}-Y_{5}, $$

where

$$ \displaystyle Y_{1} \displaystyle=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(e_{i}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}-\frac{1}{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}\right)^{2}, \displaystyle Y_{2} \displaystyle=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j\neq i}\left(e_{i}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}-\frac{1}{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}\right)W_{ij}, \displaystyle Y_{3} \displaystyle=\left(\frac{n-2}{n}\sum_{i\neq j}W_{ij}^{2}\right)-n(n-1)\alpha_{0}(1-\alpha_{0}), \displaystyle Y_{4} \displaystyle=\sum_{i,j,k,\text{ dist}}W_{ij}W_{ik}, \displaystyle Y_{5} \displaystyle=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i\neq j}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}k\neq l\\
\{k,l\}\neq\{i,j\}\end{subarray}}W_{ij}W_{kl}. $$

We now compute the mean of $Z^{*}_{n}$ . It is easy to see that

$$ \mathbb{E}[Z_{n}^{*}]=\frac{Y_{1}+\mathbb{E}[Y_{3}]}{(n-1)\alpha_{0}(1-\alpha_{0})}. $$

For $Y_{1}$ , note that $\tilde{\Omega}^{*}=\tilde{\Omega}-\mathrm{diag}(\tilde{\Omega})$ . Since $\Pi\bm{1}_{K}=\bm{1}_{n}$ , we can re-write

$$ \tilde{\Omega}=\Omega-\alpha_{0}\Pi\bm{1}_{K}\bm{1}_{K}^{\prime}\Pi^{\prime}=\Pi\left(P-\alpha_{0}\bm{1}_{K}\bm{1}_{K}^{\prime}\right)\Pi^{\prime}=\Pi M\Pi^{\prime}. $$

As a result, $\tilde{\Omega}\bm{1}_{n}=n\Pi Mh$ , and $\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}\bm{1}_{n}=0$ . We plug them into the expression of $Y_{1}$ and note that $(a+b)^{2}\geq\frac{a^{2}}{2}-b^{2}$ , for any $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$ . It follows that

$$ \displaystyle Y_{1} \displaystyle=\|\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}\|^{2}-\frac{1}{n}(\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n})^{2} \displaystyle=\|\tilde{\Omega}\bm{1}_{n}-\mathrm{diag}(\tilde{\Omega})\bm{1}_{n}\|^{2}-\frac{1}{n}(\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\mathrm{diag}(\tilde{\Omega})\bm{1}_{n})^{2} \displaystyle\geq\frac{1}{2}\|\tilde{\Omega}\bm{1}_{n}\|^{2}-\|\mathrm{diag}(\tilde{\Omega})\bm{1}_{n}\|^{2}-\frac{1}{n}(\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\mathrm{diag}(\tilde{\Omega})\bm{1}_{n})^{2} \displaystyle=\frac{n^{2}}{2}\|\Pi Mh\|^{2}-\sum_{i=1}^{n}\tilde{\Omega}^{2}_{ii}-\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\tilde{\Omega}_{ii}\right)^{2}. $$

Note that $\max_{i}|\tilde{\Omega}_{ii}|\leq\max_{k,l}|M_{kl}|=C\|M\|$ . Moreover, since $G=n^{-1}\Pi^{\prime}\Pi$ and $\lambda_{\min}(G)\geq c$ , we have $\|\Pi Mh\|^{2}=n(h^{\prime}MGMh)\geq Cn\|Mh\|^{2}$ , and $\|\Pi Mh\|^{2}\leq\|\Pi\|^{2}\|Mh\|^{2}\leq Cn\|Mh\|^{2}$ . It follows that

$$ Y_{1}=\frac{n^{2}}{2}\|\Pi Mh\|^{2}-O(n\|M\|^{2})\asymp n^{3}\|Mh\|^{2}. $$

For $Y_{3}$ , we have

$$ \mathbb{E}[Y_{3}]=\frac{n-2}{n}\sum_{i\neq j}\Omega_{ij}(1-\Omega_{ij})-n(n-1)\alpha_{0}(1-\alpha_{0}). $$

Write $\Omega_{ij}(1-\Omega_{ij})=\alpha_{0}(1-\alpha_{0})+(1-2\alpha_{0})(\Omega_{ij}-\alpha_{0})-(\Omega_{ij}-\alpha_{0})^{2}$ . Recalling that $\Omega_{ij}-\alpha_{0}=\tilde{\Omega}_{ij}$ , we plug these results into $\mathbb{E}[Y_{3}]$ to get

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[Y_{3}] \displaystyle=\frac{n-2}{n}\sum_{i\neq j}\left[\alpha_{0}(1-\alpha_{0})+(1-2\alpha_{0})\tilde{\Omega}_{ij}-\tilde{\Omega}_{ij}^{2}\right]-n(n-1)\alpha_{0}(1-\alpha_{0}) \displaystyle=-2(n-1)\alpha_{0}(1-\alpha_{0})+\frac{n-2}{n}\left[(1-2\alpha_{0})\left(\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}\bm{1}_{n}-\sum_{i}\tilde{\Omega}_{ii}\right)-\sum_{i\neq j}\tilde{\Omega}_{ij}^{2}\right] \displaystyle=-2(n-1)\alpha_{0}(1-\alpha_{0})-\frac{n-2}{n}\left[(1-2\alpha_{0})\sum_{i}\tilde{\Omega}_{ii}+\sum_{i\neq j}\tilde{\Omega}_{ij}^{2}\right]. $$

Then, $|\mathbb{E}[Y_{3}]|\leq Cn\alpha_{0}+Cn\|M\|+Cn^{2}\|M\|^{2}$ . Recall that by assumption, $\|M\|\leq C\|Mh\|$ , $n\alpha_{0}~\to~\infty$ and $\delta_{n}=n^{-3/2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}\|Mh\|^{2}\to\infty$ . It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\frac{|\mathbb{E}[Y_{3}]|}{n^{3}\|Mh\|^{2}} \displaystyle\leq\frac{C}{\sqrt{n}\delta_{n}}+\frac{C}{n^{3/4}\sqrt{n\alpha_{0}\delta_{n}}}+\frac{C}{n}\to 0. $$

It yields that

$$ \mathbb{E}[Y_{3}]=o(n^{3}\|Mh\|^{2}). $$

We plug (E.12)-(E.13) into (E.11) to get

$$ \mathbb{E}[Z_{n}^{*}]=\frac{(n/2)\|\Pi Mh\|^{2}-o(n^{3}\|Mh\|^{2})}{(n-1)\alpha_{0}(1-\alpha_{0})}\asymp n^{2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}\|Mh\|^{2}. $$

We then compute the variance of $Z_{n}^{*}$ , it is easy to see that

$$ \text{Var}(Z^{*}_{n})\leq\frac{C\text{Var}(Y_{2})+C\text{Var}(Y_{3})+C\text{Var}(Y_{4})+C\text{Var}(Y_{5})}{(n-1)^{2}\alpha_{0}^{2}(1-\alpha_{0})^{2}}. $$

By direct calculations, we know that

$$ \displaystyle\text{Var}(Y_{3}) \displaystyle\leq C\sum_{i<j}\mathbb{E}[W^{4}_{ij}]\leq C\sum_{i\neq j}\Omega_{ij}\leq Cn^{2}\alpha_{0}, \displaystyle\text{Var}(Y_{4}) \displaystyle\leq C\sum_{i,j,k\text{ dist}}\mathbb{E}[W_{ij}^{2}]\mathbb{E}[W_{ik}^{2}]\leq Cn^{3}\alpha_{0}^{2}, \displaystyle\text{Var}(Y_{5}) \displaystyle\leq\frac{C}{n^{2}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i\neq j,k\neq l\\
\{i,j\}\neq\{k,l\}\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}[W_{ij}^{2}]\mathbb{E}[W_{k,l}^{2}]\leq Cn^{2}\alpha_{0}^{2}. $$

In the previous steps, we have seen that $\tilde{\Omega}^{*}=\tilde{\Omega}-\mathrm{diag}(\tilde{\Omega})$ , $\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}\bm{1}_{n}=0$ , $\|\tilde{\Omega}\bm{1}_{n}\|^{2}=n^{3}h^{\prime}MGMh$ , $\Omega_{ij}\leq C\alpha_{0}$ , and $|\tilde{\Omega}_{ii}|\leq C\|M\|$ . It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\text{Var}(Y_{2}) \displaystyle\leq C\sum_{i\neq j}\left(e_{i}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}-\frac{1}{n}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}^{*}\bm{1}_{n}\right)^{2}\times\Omega_{ij}(1-\Omega_{ij}) \displaystyle=C\sum_{i\neq j}\left[e_{i}^{\prime}\tilde{\Omega}\bm{1}_{n}+\tilde{\Omega}_{ii}-\frac{1}{n}\left(\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\mathrm{diag}(\tilde{\Omega})\bm{1}_{n}\right)\right]^{2}\times\Omega_{ij}(1-\Omega_{ij}) \displaystyle\leq C\left[n\|\tilde{\Omega}\bm{1}_{n}\|^{2}+n\sum_{i}\tilde{\Omega}_{ii}^{2}+\left(\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\mathrm{diag}(\tilde{\Omega})\bm{1}_{n}\right)^{2}\right]\times C\alpha_{0} \displaystyle\leq Cn^{4}\alpha_{0}\|Mh\|^{2}+Cn^{2}\alpha_{0}\|\mathrm{diag}(M)\|^{2} \displaystyle\leq Cn^{4}\alpha_{0}\|Mh\|^{2}. $$

We combine the above results and note that for $n$ big enough, $n\alpha_{0}\geq c$ . It gives

$$ \displaystyle\text{Var}(Z^{*}_{n}) \displaystyle\leq\frac{C}{n^{2}\alpha_{0}^{2}}\left(n^{4}\alpha_{0}\|Mh\|^{2}+n^{3}\alpha_{0}^{2}\right) \displaystyle\leq Cn^{2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}\|Mh\|^{2}+Cn. $$

In conclusion, the mean and variance of $Z_{n}^{*}$ are characterized by (E.14) and (E.15), respectively.

The mean and variance of $\psi_{n}^{DC}$ . We now show the claims of this theorem. First, consider the mean of $\psi_{n}^{DC}$ . Recalling (E.1) and letting $\Delta_{n}=(1+U_{n})^{-1}U_{n}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\sqrt{n}\,\mathbb{E}[\psi^{DC}_{n}] \displaystyle\geq\mathbb{E}[Z_{n}^{*}]-\mathbb{E}\Bigl|\frac{U_{n}}{1+U_{n}}Z_{n}^{*}\Bigr|-n\,\mathbb{E}\Bigl|\frac{U_{n}}{1+U_{n}}\Bigr| \displaystyle\geq\mathbb{E}[Z_{n}^{*}]-\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{n}^{2}]}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(Z_{n}^{*})^{2}]}-n\sqrt{\mathbb{E}[\Delta^{2}_{n}]}. $$

The mean and variance of $Z_{n}^{*}$ have been analyzed above. We now study $\Delta_{n}$ , which is a function of $\hat{\alpha}_{n}$ and $\alpha_{0}$ . Note that

$$ \max_{i,j}\Omega_{ij}\leq\max_{k,\ell}P_{k\ell}\leq\bm{1}_{K}^{\prime}P\bm{1}_{K}\leq Ch^{\prime}Ph=C\alpha_{0}, $$

where $\bm{1}_{K}^{\prime}P\bm{1}_{K}\leq Ch^{\prime}Ph$ is because $\min_{k}h_{k}\geq c$ . Since $\hat{\alpha}_{n}=\frac{1}{n(n-1)}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}A\bm{1}_{n}$ and $\alpha_{0}=h^{\prime}Ph=n^{-2}\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\Omega\bm{1}_{n}$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\left|\mathbb{E}[\hat{\alpha}_{n}]-\alpha_{0}\right| \displaystyle=\frac{1}{n(n-1)}\left|\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\Omega\bm{1}_{n}-\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\mathrm{diag}(\Omega)\bm{1}_{n}-n(n-1)\alpha_{0}\right| \displaystyle=\frac{1}{n(n-1)}\left|n^{2}\alpha_{0}-\bm{1}_{n}^{\prime}\mathrm{diag}(\Omega)\bm{1}_{n}-n(n-1)\alpha_{0}\right|\;\;\leq Cn^{-1}\alpha_{0}, \displaystyle\text{Var}(\hat{\alpha}_{n}) \displaystyle=\frac{4}{n^{2}(n-1)^{2}}\sum_{i<j}\Omega_{ij}(1-\Omega_{ij})\;\;\leq Cn^{-2}\alpha_{0}. $$

Furthermore, we write $\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\mathbb{E}[\hat{\alpha}_{n}]=\frac{2}{n(n-1)}\sum_{i<j}W_{ij}$ , where $\{W_{ij}\}_{i<j}$ is a collection of independent, bounded, zero-mean variables. We apply Bernstein’s inequality and use (E.19) to get

$$ \mathbb{P}\bigl(\bigl|\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\mathbb{E}[\alpha_{n}]\bigr|>t\bigr)\leq\exp\biggl(-\frac{t^{2}/2}{Cn^{-2}\alpha_{0}+Cn^{-2}t}\biggr),\qquad\mbox{for all }t>0. $$

Consider the event $E=\{|\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\alpha_{0}|<\delta\cdot\alpha_{0}\}$ , for a sufficiently small constant $\delta>0$ to be determined. Using the above inequality, $\mathbb{P}(E^{c})\leq\exp(-C\delta\cdot n^{2}\alpha_{0})$ for big enough $n$ . On the event $E$ , we can derive a bound for $|\Delta_{n}|$ . Recalling that $U_{n}=\frac{\hat{\alpha}_{n}(1-\hat{\alpha}_{n})}{\alpha_{0}(1-\alpha_{0})}$ , we have

$$ \Delta_{n}=\frac{U_{n}}{1+U_{n}}=\frac{(\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\alpha_{0})(1-\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\alpha_{0})}{\hat{\alpha}_{n}(1-\hat{\alpha}_{n})}. $$

Since $\alpha_{0}\leq 1-c$ for a constant $c\in(0,1)$ , when $\delta$ is chosen properly small, $|\Delta_{n}|\leq C\alpha_{0}^{-1}|\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\alpha_{0}|$ on the event $E$ , where the constant $C>0$ here does not depend on $\delta$ . On the event $E^{c}$ , according to the footnote on Page 3, $|\Delta_{n}|\leq Cn^{2}$ . It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{n}^{2}] \displaystyle\leq Cn^{4}\cdot\mathbb{P}(E^{c})+C\alpha_{0}^{-2}\mathbb{E}[(\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\alpha_{0})^{2}] \displaystyle\leq Cn^{4}\cdot\mathbb{P}(E^{c})+C\alpha_{0}^{-2}\bigl[(\mathbb{E}[\hat{\alpha}_{n}]-\alpha_{0})^{2}+\text{Var}(\hat{\alpha}_{n})\bigr] \displaystyle\leq Cn^{4}\exp(-C\delta n^{2}\alpha_{0})+C\alpha_{0}^{-2}(n^{-2}\alpha_{0}^{2}+n^{-2}\alpha_{0}) \displaystyle\leq Cn^{-2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}. $$

We plug (E.23) into (E.17) and then utilize (E.14)-(E.15). Recalling that we have defined $\delta_{n}=n^{3/2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}\|Mh\|^{2}$ , it yields that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\psi_{n}^{DC}] \displaystyle\geq\frac{C}{\sqrt{n}}\biggl(n^{2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}\|Mh\|^{2}-\sqrt{Cn^{-2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}}\times \displaystyle\sqrt{(n^{2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}\|Mh\|^{2})^{2}+\bigl(n^{2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}\|Mh\|^{2}+n\bigr)}-n\sqrt{Cn^{-2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}}\biggr) \displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}=\frac{C}{\sqrt{n}}\biggl(\sqrt{n}\delta_{n}-\sqrt{Cn^{-2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}}\sqrt{n\delta_{n}^{2}+\sqrt{n}\delta_{n}+n}-n\sqrt{Cn^{-2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}}\biggr)} \displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\geq C\delta_{n}\left(1-\frac{C}{\sqrt{n^{2}\alpha_{0}}}-\frac{C}{\sqrt{n^{5/2}\alpha_{0}\delta_{n}}}-\frac{C}{\sqrt{n^{2}\alpha_{0}\delta_{n}^{2}}}\right)-\frac{C}{\sqrt{n\alpha_{0}}}} \displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\geq C\delta_{n}\Bigl[1-O\bigl(n^{-5/4}\alpha_{0}^{-1/2}\delta_{n}^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\alpha_{0}^{-1/2}\delta_{n}^{-1}\bigr)\Bigr]-O\bigl(n^{-1/2}\alpha_{0}^{-1/2}\bigr).} $$

Now, assume that $\delta_{n}\geq C$ . Then, there exists a constant $c_{1}>0$ such that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\psi_{n}^{DC}]\geq c_{1}\delta_{n}-O\bigl(n^{-1/2}\alpha_{0}^{-1/2}\bigr). $$

This gives the first claim.

Next, consider the variance of $\psi_{n}^{DC}$ . Note that $(1+U_{n})^{-1}=1-\Delta_{n}$ and $(1+U_{n})^{-1}U_{n}=\Delta_{n}$ . It follows from (E.1) that $\sqrt{n}\,\psi_{n}^{DC}=Z^{*}_{n}-\Delta_{n}Z^{*}_{n}-n\Delta_{n}$ . Therefore,

$$ \displaystyle\text{Var}(\psi_{n}^{DC}) \displaystyle\leq Cn^{-1}[\text{Var}(Z^{*}_{n})+\text{Var}(\Delta_{n}Z^{*}_{n})+n^{2}\text{Var}(\Delta_{n})] \displaystyle\leq Cn^{-1}\bigl(\text{Var}(Z^{*}_{n})+\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{n}^{2}(Z^{*}_{n})^{2}]+n^{2}\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{n}^{2}]\bigr) \displaystyle\leq Cn^{-1}\Bigl(n^{2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}\|Mh\|^{2}+n+\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{n}^{2}(Z^{*}_{n})^{2}]+\alpha_{0}^{-1}\Bigr), $$

where we have used (E.15) and (E.23) in the last inequality.

We calculate $\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{n}^{2}(Z^{*}_{n})^{2}]$ . For a large enough constant $B_{0}>0$ , we define an event

$$ E_{1}=\bigl\{|\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\mathbb{E}[\hat{\alpha}_{n}]|\leq B_{0}n^{-1}\sqrt{\alpha_{0}\log(n)}\bigr\}. $$

By (E.22), $\mathbb{P}(E_{1}^{c})\leq\exp(-B\log(n))$ , where the constant $B>0$ is a monotone increasing function of $B_{0}$ . With a properly large $B_{0}$ , we can make $\exp(-B\log(n))=o(n^{8}\alpha_{0}^{-2})$ . Now, on the event $E_{1}$ , we have $|\Delta_{n}|\leq C\alpha_{0}^{-1}|\hat{\alpha}_{n}-\alpha_{0}|\leq Cn^{-1}\alpha_{0}^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log(n)}$ . On the event $E^{c}$ , we note that $|\Delta_{n}|\leq Cn^{2}$ and $|Z_{n}^{*}|\leq Cn^{2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}$ hold uniformly. It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{n}^{2}(Z^{*}_{n})^{2}] \displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{n}^{2}(Z^{*}_{n})^{2}\cdot I_{E_{1}^{c}}]+\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{n}^{2}(Z^{*}_{n})^{2}\cdot I_{E_{1}}] \displaystyle\leq Cn^{8}\alpha_{0}^{-2}\cdot\exp(-B\log(n))+Cn^{-2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}\log(n)\mathbb{E}\bigl[(Z_{n}^{*})^{2}\cdot I_{E^{c}}\bigr] \displaystyle\leq o(1)+Cn^{-2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}\log(n)\bigl[(\mathbb{E}[Z_{n}^{*}])^{2}+\text{Var}(Z_{n}^{*})\bigr] \displaystyle\leq o(1)+\frac{C\log(n)}{n^{2}\alpha_{0}}\Bigl[(n^{2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}\|Mh\|^{2})^{2}+n^{2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}\|Mh\|^{2}+n\Bigr], $$

where in the last inequality we have used (E.14)-(E.15). We plug (E.31) into (E.28) to get

$$ \displaystyle\text{Var}(\psi_{n}^{DC}) \displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\leq C\Bigl(1+n^{-1}\alpha_{0}^{-1}+n^{-1/2}\delta_{n}+\frac{\log(n)}{n^{3}\alpha_{0}}(n\delta_{n}^{2}+\sqrt{n}\delta_{n}+n)\Bigr)} \displaystyle\leq C\Bigl[1+n^{-1/2}\delta_{n}+n^{-2}\alpha_{0}^{-1}\delta_{n}^{2}\log(n)\Bigr]. $$

This gives the second claim. ∎

In preparation, we derive some useful results. First, we study $|\overline{\Omega}_{ij}|$ . Write $M=P-\alpha_{0}\bm{1}_{K}\bm{1}_{K}^{\prime}$ . Then,

$$ \displaystyle|\alpha_{1}-\alpha_{0}| \displaystyle=|\mathbb{E}[\hat{\alpha}_{n}]-\alpha_{0}|=\left|\frac{1}{n(n-1)}\sum_{i\neq j}\pi_{i}^{\prime}M\pi_{j}\right| \displaystyle=\left|\frac{1}{n(n-1)}\sum_{i,j}\pi_{i}^{\prime}M\pi_{j}-\frac{1}{n(n-1)}\sum_{i}\pi_{i}^{\prime}M\pi_{i}\right| \displaystyle\leq\frac{n}{n-1}\left|h^{\prime}Mh\right|+\frac{\|M\|}{n-1}\leq\frac{C\|M\|}{n}, $$

where we have used in the last line that $h^{\prime}Mh=h^{\prime}Ph-\alpha_{0}h^{\prime}\bm{1}_{K}\bm{1}_{K}^{\prime}h=0$ .

Note that $\overline{\Omega}_{ij}=\pi_{i}^{\prime}P\pi_{j}-\alpha_{1}=\pi_{i}^{\prime}M\pi_{j}+\alpha_{0}-\alpha_{1}$ . It follows that

$$ |\overline{\Omega}_{ij}|\leq|\pi_{i}^{\prime}M\pi_{j}|+|\alpha_{0}-\alpha_{1}|\leq C\|M\|. $$

Next, we study $\Delta_{n}$ . By definition,

$$ \Delta_{n}=\mathbb{E}[\hat{\alpha}_{n}]-\hat{\alpha}_{n}=-\frac{1}{n(n-1)}\sum_{i\neq j}(A_{ij}-\Omega_{ij})=-\frac{1}{n(n-1)}\sum_{i\neq j}W_{ij}. $$

Using properties of Bernoulli variables, we have $\mathbb{E}[W_{ij}^{2}]=\Omega_{ij}(1-\Omega_{ij})\leq\Omega_{ij}$ and $|\mathbb{E}[W_{ij}^{m}]|\leq C\Omega_{ij}$ , for any fixed $m\geq 3$ (the constant $C$ may depend on $m$ ). Note that

$$ \Omega_{ij}=\pi_{i}^{\prime}P\pi_{j}\leq\bm{1}_{K}^{\prime}P\bm{1}_{K}\leq C\alpha_{0}, $$

where we have used that $\min_{k}h_{k}>C/K$ , which is a consequence of (3.4). Additionally,

$$ \sum_{i,j}\Omega_{ij}=\sum_{i,j}\pi_{i}^{\prime}P\pi_{j}=n^{2}h^{\prime}Ph=n^{2}\alpha_{0}. $$

It follows that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{n}^{2}] \displaystyle=\frac{4}{n^{2}(n-1)^{2}}\sum_{i<j}\mathbb{E}(W^{2}_{ij})\leq Cn^{-4}\sum_{i\neq j}\Omega_{ij}\leq Cn^{-2}\alpha_{0}, \displaystyle|\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{n}^{3}]| \displaystyle=\frac{8}{n^{3}(n-1)^{3}}\biggl|\mathbb{E}\biggl[\sum_{i<j,k<l,u<v}W_{ij}W_{kl}W_{uv}\biggr]\biggr|=\frac{8}{n^{3}(n-1)^{3}}\biggl|\mathbb{E}\biggl[\sum_{i<j}W_{ij}^{3}\biggr]\biggr| \displaystyle\leq Cn^{-6}\sum_{i<j}\Omega_{ij}\;\leq\;Cn^{-4}\alpha_{0}, \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{n}^{4}] \displaystyle=\frac{16}{n^{4}(n-1)^{4}}\Biggl(\sum_{i<j}\mathbb{E}[W_{ij}^{4}]+3\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}i<j,k<l\\
(i,j)\neq(k,l)\end{subarray}}\mathbb{E}[W_{ij}^{2}]\mathbb{E}[W_{kl}^{2}]\Biggr) \displaystyle\leq Cn^{-8}\Biggl[\sum_{i<j}\Omega_{ij}+\Bigl(\sum_{i<j}\Omega_{ij}\Bigr)\Bigl(\sum_{k<\ell}\Omega_{k\ell}\Bigr)\Biggr]\leq Cn^{-4}\alpha_{0}^{2}, \displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{n}^{8}] \displaystyle\leq Cn^{-16}\Biggl(\sum_{i<j,k<l,m<s,q<t}\mathbb{E}[W^{2}_{ij}]\mathbb{E}[W^{2}_{kl}]\mathbb{E}[W^{2}_{ms}]\mathbb{E}[W^{2}_{qt}]\Biggr) \displaystyle\leq Cn^{-16}\Bigl(\sum_{i<j}\Omega_{ij}\Bigr)^{4}\leq Cn^{-8}\alpha_{0}^{4}. $$

We shall frequently use (F.4) and (F.5) in the proof below.

$$ \mathbb{E}[X_{1}]=0. $$
